# Preface
## To the
### Understanding Lover of the Golden Art.

<note>The "Golden Art" is a traditional term for alchemy, the practice of attempting to transform base metals into gold and seeking the "Philosopher's Stone."</note>

When it is in no way to be expected from wise, rational, and upright persons that they would bring forth foolish, impossible things that run against nature, and present them to others as believable and true—much less write and teach extensively about them—it might seem to many a strange and absurd thing that one is once again bringing to light and sending to print such an extensive and detailed description of the so-highly doubted Golden Art <note>alchemy</note> of transforming lesser metals into gold and silver. 

For what could be more beautifully formed and described than finding here (as the title states) the **Golden Fleece** <note>original: "AUREUM VELLUS"</note>, so highly praised by the ancient philosophers <note>In alchemical texts, "Philosophers" refers to the historical masters of the craft, such as Hermes Trismegistus or Geber.</note> and conquered with much effort? How a golden treasure and art-chamber is thereby opened, in which are contained and brought together the writings and books of the most noble, most excellent, select, magnificent, and proven authors, drawn from the ancient, surviving, and preserved relics and monuments of the philosophers from past and recent times? 

These have been published most faithfully from the originals, since the first edition <note>original: "Edition"</note> from the year 1598 <note>original: "Anno 1598"</note>, printed at Rorschach on Lake Constance and at Basel in 1604, is so rare and difficult to obtain that the publisher had to procure it at extraordinary cost. He has done so to awaken even greater pleasure in the lovers of this science (after having previously released so many other books of the same kind). All of this, however, might be viewed poorly by the untimely critics—those who very quickly despise what they cannot understand or grasp, or because they, being on the wrong path, [seek] this jewel...

<summary>This preface introduces a collection of alchemical texts titled "Aureum Vellus" (The Golden Fleece), defending the legitimacy of alchemy against skeptics and explaining the rarity of this specific edition.</summary>

...to grasp / [and who] have perhaps happened upon [this work] / and have already given up as lost all hope of a successful conclusion and possession of these secrets) [this work] might be viewed as an unnecessary, even misleading labor. This is especially true since, after so much effort and unspeakable costs which the lovers and seekers of the <term>Philosopher's Stone</term> <note>The legendary substance believed to be capable of turning base metals into gold and silver, and sometimes acting as an elixir of life.</note> have applied everywhere, nothing has yet come to light that would grant the skeptical world even a glimpse of the possibility. Instead, the many legends and histories of transformations occurring here and there are always entangled with such doubtful circumstances, as if the whole thing were composed and fabricated from fables and fairy tales by gold-greedy minds.

Added to this is the insurmountable difficulty of such a vexing undertaking, as the matter is nowhere described so clearly and distinctly that one could make a reliable calculation of profit from it; indeed, all the highly praised gold-making processes often do not even pay for the lead used for testing, or bring the slightest advantage. The words uttered by the Philosophers <note>In this context, "Philosophers" refers to historical alchemists and masters of the "Hermetic" arts.</note> and teachers of the art in their writings are entirely like riddles, as they themselves remind us: wherever they name a thing clearly, they mean something else entirely. Everything must be taken and <term>judged</term> <note>original: "dijudicirt"; to discern or evaluate with wisdom and caution.</note> not according to the literal word, but according to the inner meaning.

Who then, without reason—like a blind person—thinks they will hit the mark in this difficult investigation? What kind of luck could they expect from such errors? That all the details have not been described so clearly by the masters of this art does not arise from any malice or wicked intent to lead others astray, deceive them, or cause them harm. Rather, Divine Providence and foresight—which governs the world with the highest wisdom—has introduced this marvelous order (as is well noted here on pages 24 and 58), so that people should not all be equally rich or of the same wealth. For otherwise, a theater of <term>extravagance</term> <note>original: "Uppigkeit"; implying luxury, decadence, or social excess that disrupts order.</note>, vice, and lack of virtue would emerge, where no one would show the slightest compliance to another, nor be forced to recognize any person as higher or more worthy. What wonder is it then, that those who attained certain knowledge of these secrets wrote so hiddenly and darkly about them?

# Preface.
->a 3<-

<meta>catchword: -aries</meta>

[It is for] God alone to give knowledge of this to someone, as it only happens to those who are researchers and lovers of Divine Truth, but not to misers who deal in fraud, nor to idlers who want to get rich in their sleep and have no desire to work, and even less to those minds devoted to worldly pleasures; for to all these, heaven is locked. Even if they had all the Hermetic books to be found in the world together, and set up ever so many <term>laboratories</term>, smelting, <term>digestion</term>, and <term>distillation furnaces</term> for that purpose, they would accomplish nothing with them, but would only be brought into greater confusion thereby. 

But for what purpose (an inexperienced person might burst out in impatience) do all the piled-up writings of so many <term>alchemists</term> serve? It would be better to touch or read nothing of it; for since one can gain no understanding from it to produce gold or silver anywhere, it would indeed be much better to keep such artistic feats secret than to publish such shapeless processes and offer them for sale publicly. 

But just as there are two kinds of lovers (as already mentioned), the worthy and the unworthy <note>original: "Digni & Indigni"</note>, the former will nonetheless see a light in the deepest darkness, by which they can arrange their work and investigation, while the latter will grope around in the dark even at high noon, mistaking one thing for another <note>original: "quid pro quo"; literally "this for that," referring here to the confusion of materials or principles.</note>. It is enough that the connoisseurs of truth understand one another, while the so-called "vain ash-blowers" <note>A derogatory term for "puffers," or amateur alchemists who obsessively blew at their charcoal fires without understanding the spiritual or chemical principles involved.</note> with their Babylonian language—where none can guess the other's meaning—ever expand their numbers; and since they can achieve nothing according to perfection, they resort to sophistry, where refined calamine and zinc provide the color of gold, and adulterated tin and copper must resemble silver. 

The guideline for extricating oneself from this deceptive labyrinth will therefore primarily aim at first distinguishing well whether those who have presented themselves as masters of the golden art and written books about it were of sound mind, and did not perhaps delude themselves with vain imagination—as an incredible multitude of them exist who, when they have barely begun, pledge body and soul with great oaths that they shall not fail. Secondly, [distinguish those who] have attained a complete experience of the matter and have not remained stuck merely in theory. Thirdly, those who show a sincere mind and, having known the art, nevertheless had no desire to mislead others through false teaching, nor to offer themselves for hire, whether to great lords or other wealthy persons. And fourthly, those who duly refrain from boasting and grand bragging about how they can immediately produce millions with their <term>tincture</term> <note>A substance, often the Philosopher's Stone in liquid form, capable of transmuting metals or curing illness.</note> and can infallibly cure <note>original: "curiren"</note> all diseases, and in this respect [keep within] the bound-

<summary>This page warns that alchemical success is a gift from God reserved for the moral and diligent, while dismissing "puffers" and frauds who use sophisticated language to mask their failures. It provides four criteria for identifying a true master of the art: sound mind, practical experience, sincerity, and humility.</summary>

# Preface.

<meta>catchword: Die</meta>

[...do] not overstep the boundaries of modesty. All of those [worthy authors] can surely be trusted most safely, and no harm is to be feared from following them; whereas, on the contrary, the greatest number of daring gold-makers ultimately end in ignorance, presumption, deception, and boasting, as daily experience testifies. In this <note>original: "Seculo de aurato, nondum aureo"</note> gilded age—though not yet a golden one—they have made themselves so hated that they are viewed by most people more as useless coal-burners <note>A derogatory term for failed alchemists who spent all their money on charcoal for their furnaces without result.</note> than as true <term>gold-artists</term> <note>A term for practitioners of alchemy who sought the transformation of metals.</note>. 

The authors cited and collected in this book of the **Golden Fleece** consistently exhibit (albeit mixed with some errors) the four aforementioned qualities. They are presented as the most excellent, experienced, and proven writers, who at the very least knew such <term>particulars</term> <note>Specific chemical recipes or "small" transmutations that work on a limited scale.</note> as could later provide a certain guide to the <term>universal</term> <note>The "Universal Work," or the creation of the Philosopher's Stone, which was believed to transmute any metal and cure all illness.</note>. Because these authors base themselves on the experience of the ancient Egyptians, Chaldeans, and Arabs, they are to be held in higher esteem than the blindly guessed conjectures of untimely newcomers. Therefore, for a better explanation of the matter, it may not be inappropriate to append a brief report on these proven practitioners—how their operations agree with the truth or depart from it. 

This is not so that the reader of these writings, as a lover of the Art, may immediately hope to become a possessor of the **Golden Fleece** and be clothed with the wool of the <term>Martial Ram</term> <note>In alchemy, the Ram (Aries) is the zodiac sign associated with the beginning of the Great Work in spring; "Martial" refers to the use of iron (Mars) in the process.</note>; for the laws of this <note>original: "Ordinis Beneficentissimi"</note> **Most Beneficent Order** do not allow for this, nor would the authors who have written of it claim or approve it. Rather, it is simply to show that the golden Art proceeds on steady feet; for whoever takes the right path according to their warning may, from the golden <term>triumph-chariot</term> <note>A reference to the "Triumphal Chariot of Antimony," a famous alchemical text by Basil Valentine.</note>, at least reach a small goal. The entire work is divided into five different treatises for this purpose, so that the distinction between the various artistic efforts may be better recognized, and the apprentice may have the opportunity to choose the most suitable method. 

<margin>p. 1.</margin>
The fortunate <term>Salomon Trismosin</term> (meaning "the triple tower" in Greek) makes the beginning here. It is from him that <term>Theophrastus Paracelsus</term> <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus (1493–1541), the most famous physician-alchemist of the Renaissance.</note> is said to have learned the foundation of his science. His travels with the three powerful <term>tinctures</term> he discovered are worth contemplating. The <term>Red Lion</term>, the <term>Mercurial Water</term> in which gold is said to be reduced to its "first matter," and the <term>Black Eagle</term> and its oil for "cementing" <note>A process of refining gold by heating it with other substances to remove impurities.</note> are incomparable in their effect, should such a result follow as is attributed to them. Noteworthy is the downfall of the Venetian nobleman on page 4, who perhaps misused this Art. The medicinal power to renew life on page 9 surpasses all other means.

# Preface.

<meta>catchword: through</meta>

The **Copulation** <note>In alchemy, the "union" or joining of two substances, often symbolized as a marriage.</note> or first beginning of the metals by **Hieronymus Crinot**, serving as an introduction to the **Universal Tincture**, along with the **Alphabet** found among the treasure of the **Egyptian books** within the **Trismosinian writings**, may awaken many speculations among enthusiasts as to how the Art was also put into practice among the heathens and unbelievers. However, what is reported concerning the <term>mine-damp</term> <note>original: "Bergschwaden"; a vaporous substance found in mines, which alchemists believed was a raw, spiritual form of Mercury.</note> on page 16—which, when brought to its hardness as a **Mercury of the Philosophers**, is said to yield the sought-after **Sulfur** through the help of the **Sun** <note>Symbol for Gold</note> and the **Moon** <note>Symbol for Silver</note>—has turned many alchemists into "young lions" who subsequently smeared themselves with <term>Gur</term> <note>A term for a "primordial juice" or metallic "embryo" found in the earth, thought to be the raw material from which metals grow.</note>. The manuscript of **Biltdorffer** agrees with this, and the **three Augmentations** may also yield their own benefit. The Tincture of the Egyptian King **Xophar** on page 33 is not entirely unlike the description given by **Lully** <note>Ramon Llull, a major figure in medieval logic and alchemy.</note>. The secret of King **Xopholat**, which is said to have extended his life to 300 years, prepared from the golden **Mountain-Sulfur**, is not to be despised precisely because of its simplicity. The **nine Tinctures** that proceed from a single root—where salts are drawn from the metals to prepare the **Stone** <note>The Philosopher's Stone</note>—indicate various manual techniques that can be useful for this hidden work. The **Red Eagle** of **Trismosinos**, made from the vapor of silver, which he saw in the possession of an Egyptian, is of a very secret nature, in that it transforms the lesser metals into gold and makes white gemstones unspeakably brilliant, while also turning the reddest gold into pure, clear silver. The eight Tinctures that follow seem, according to their preparation, not to be of the best kind, as he restricts several of them to specific days of the year. **Salt Nefolon**, made from the sharpest **Salt of Tartar** <note>Potassium carbonate</note> with **Spirit of Wine** <note>Alcohol</note> to reduce gold, has already been noted by many. The **English Tincture** from **Antimony** has this particular quality: that many materials used by artists are rejected as useless, for in antimony <note>original: "Spießglas"</note> and its sulfur the "darkened sun" of gold is said to be hidden, so that whoever can achieve the separation from it will find a livelihood therein. How the process must be arranged can be read at length on page 71 and following. The subsequent Tinctures, which are said to contain secrets beyond all <term>Arcana</term> <note>Deep medicinal or chemical mysteries.</note>, as well as those from **sulfurous pyrites** and **flint**, and how they are to be used in the Chemical Art, as well as how to fix <term>Usukur</term> <note>Likely a reference to cinnabar or a similar red mineral.</note> with **Oil of Saturn** <note>Lead</note>, can be set forth for trial; and this is, in brief, the content of the first treatise.

In the second part, the most distinguished writings, tinctures, and processes of the famous **Theophrastus Paracelsus**, which have never before been seen in print, are presented. His **Dialogue on Alchemy** with **Chrysophilus** <note>A name meaning "Gold-Lover."</note> aims to demonstrate the restoration of born things to their origin, and how successfully the metals there...

# Preface.

...through can be transformed. Among other things, on page 105, the history of the invention of the Alchemical Art among the Greeks is presented, specifically regarding Jason’s expedition to Colchis, where it is indicated what the Golden Fleece <note>original: "guldene Vellus oder Vließ"</note> actually was. Lastly, the signs provided on page 107 for how one should distinguish sophistical <note>Deceptive or fraudulent works</note> books from the true ones are not exactly the best he cites. Lully <note>Ramon Llull, a major medieval philosopher often credited with alchemical works he likely did not write.</note>, whom he (as it appears) never read, is censured by him for daring to interpret the books of ancient writers; the rest of the discussion serves the matter little. His elixir, which is meant to cure leprosy, gout <note>original: "Podagram"</note>, dropsy, stroke, etc., might perhaps be of a superior kind. How to prepare **potable gold** <note>original: "Aurum potabile"; a medicinal liquid believed to have life-extending properties.</note> is not fully shown. The Paracelsian tinctures—how the seed is to be sown in the earth, how mercury <note>symbolized in original by ☿</note> can be coagulated into gold <note>symbolized in original by ☉</note> through the salts of metals, and how to bring forth the Green Lion <note>An alchemical term often referring to strong acids or the raw material for the Philosophers' Stone.</note>—are nearly invalid processes.

<margin>theophr.</margin>
This Theophrastus <note>Theophrastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus.</note> certainly had many enemies in his time who blackened his name most severely and described him so poorly that one might think no greater idiot was to be found in medicine and alchemy. He did, however, perform many extraordinary cures. Yet, he himself denies that he was in possession of the **Philosophers' Stone** <note>original: "Lapidem Philosophorum"</note>, even though in some parts of his writings he boasts significantly about how he buried an unspeakable treasure that would be discovered in his own time. His last will and testament, as attested by the notaries, contains only meager items. The epitaph, or the gravestone inscription, set for him is more flattering than what he was actually able to perform. The writings often attributed to his name contain many superstitious, absurd things, especially when he attempts to mix in matters of mathematics and astronomy. Among recent writers, almost no one has depicted or described him more hideously than Conringius <note>Hermann Conring, a famous 17th-century physician and scholar at the University of Helmstedt.</note>, Professor at Helmstedt, who calls him a "monster of a man" <note>original: "Monstrum hominis"</note> "born for the destruction of better learning" <note>original: "in perniciem melioris eruditionis natum"</note>; nevertheless, he must admit that some very good medicines are found in his writings. The "augmentation" <note>A process meant to increase the volume or potency of a metallic substance.</note> with the Mercury of Lead <note>original: "Saturno Mercurij"</note>, which is also said to originate from Theophrastus and was later published by the famous Abbot Johannes Trithemius, will hardly produce the effect attributed to it on page 126. The Spiritual Sun of Bartholomeus Korndorffer, the two philosophical figures, the "Viscous Well" or "Graduation-Water"—in which fine silver is supposedly graded <note>Transformed or purified to a higher state.</note> into good gold within four hours—and other such things are merely "particulars" <note>Alchemical processes that only work on a small scale or are incomplete.</note>. Indeed, the well-known Dr. Becher <note>Johann Joachim Becher, a prominent chemist and advisor to the Emperor.</note> has already specified a good portion of these Korndorfferian experiments in his *Chemical Lucky-Harbor* <note>original: "Chymischen Glücks-Hafen"</note>, though they are described here much better and more completely. The old monks' processes for transforming silver into gold on page 153 contain much the same...

# Preface.

...does not sting. <note>This phrase likely completes a sentence from the previous page, possibly referring to the quality of a medicinal preparation.</note> The inextinguishable, burning lights of Trithemius <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), an abbot and scholar famous for his works on cryptography and the occult.</note>, for which Emperor Maximilian is said to have gifted him 6,000 crowns, will require another additive in the Practice <note>The practical, laboratory-based application of alchemy.</note>, for oil of sulfur prepared in the described manner will not prove itself to be so incombustible.

In the third treatise is found the old Alchemical Script <note>original: "Scriptum Alchymisticum"</note> titled *The Splendor of the Sun* <note>original: "Splendor Solis"; one of the most famous and beautifully illustrated alchemical manuscripts.</note> or *The Radiance of the Sun*, separated into seven parts with its many strange figures. It is, however, to be regarded more as a darkened sun, because the description is intended for those who already have knowledge of the matter. *The Mirror of Alchemy* by Poyselius <note>Caspar Poyselius, a 16th-century alchemist.</note> regarding the origin of metals and the first matter of the stone <note>original: "prima Materia Lapidis"</note> proceeds in a more understandable and better fashion; just as he rejects plants, minerals, and metals—even the perfect ones like gold and silver <note>The original uses the symbols ☉ and ☽</note>—for that end, so he teaches that one may yet find bodies that contain within themselves a purified mercury and sulfur, in which nature has worked so little that one may accomplish the full decoction, purification, separation, and fixation with artificial and moderate fire. (page 221). *The Key to Chemical Maneuvers* consists of thirteen special preparations, followed by all sorts of particulars <note>Minor alchemical operations or transmutations of specific metals.</note>; anyone will be able to learn these without difficulty and experience how they accord with the truth. The *Process for the Tincture upon the Mercury of the Sun and Moon* <note>The "Mercury of the Sun and Moon" refers to mercury derived from or intended to act upon gold and silver.</note> is more sophistical <note>Deceptive or logically flawed.</note> than according to the Art, yet it can have its uses in other things. The *Dialogue of Philosophy* is composed only in poor terms. The *Twelve Chapters on the Philosophers' Stone* are arranged according to the old, customary manner. The *Philosophical Work and Conversation of the Yellow and Red Man* by Cardinal Melchior <note>Melchior Cibinensis, a clergyman who wrote alchemical processes in the form of a Mass.</note> is indeed found in many alchemical books, but is expressed here most completely, although the meaning of the words is quite obscure. The *Various Philosophical Writings* (page 307) are useful to know, as some things are mentioned therein that may help in the explanation of the secret <note>original: "Arcani"</note>. The *Treatise on the Fifth Essence of Wine* <note>original: "de Quinta Essentia Vini"</note> shows the way in which the so-called vegetable mercury <note>A solvent, often highly rectified alcohol, believed to have the power to extract the "sulfur" or essence of metals.</note> is to be prepared, which Lully, Basil, and others exalt very highly and cite as a key to drawing the sulfur out of the best metals, although they are not at all in agreement regarding the method of bringing it out of the wine. The *Emerald Tablet of Hermes* <note>The "Tabula Smaragdina," a foundational Hermetic text containing the famous maxim "As above, so below."</note> is well known, but the interpretation requires minds that can turn the uppermost down and vice-versa.

In the fourth treatise, there are once again various philosophical and spagyric <note>Alchemical medicine involving the separation and recombination of plant or mineral constituents.</note> writings; first, Caspar Hartung von Hoff’s explanation of the preparation of the Stone, together with its subject, its nature, and essence, proven with Holy Scripture...

# Preface.

...worth reading. He addresses those who seek it in unseemly things very harshly, decrying it as roguery and thievery when they look for it in wine, nitric acid <note>original: "Aquafort"</note>, urine <note>original: "Harn"</note>, common mercury, common sulfur, salt, etc. Since, in his opinion, mercury <term>☿</term> <note>The chemical symbol for mercury, often representing the "spirit" of a substance in alchemy.</note> cannot be named or understood as anything other than the "Green Lion" <note>A common alchemical term for acidic vitriol or a specific state of raw mineral mercury.</note>, which he calls Vultimori or Vitriol <note>original: "Vitriolum"</note> on page 355. Regarding the colors, names, and the nature of the Noble Stone, he makes—after his own imaginative fashion—many exclamations, which, however, are of little help here. The old rhymes on the *First Matter of the Philosophers* <note>original: "de prima Materia Philosophorum"</note>, on composition, augmentation, etc., along with the interpretation of the Hermetic Painting on page 337, reveal how the ingenious laboratory workers composed poetic concepts about their work at the fire; these are not all to be entirely rejected. 

The complete report and practical instructions by an anonymous author <note>original: "Anonymi"</note> which follows is based on a true, beautiful marcasite <note>A mineral, often iron pyrite, which alchemists believed contained the "seed" of gold.</note> in which natural gold grows. How one is to proceed with it and what shall follow is left to the reader’s judgment, for many strange things are contained within marcasites. *The Book of Secrets* by John of Padua is filled with processes in the style of how the monks labored in the monasteries. King Solomon and the Patriarchs are also said to have had knowledge of this Art <note>Referring to Alchemy, often called the "Sacred Art."</note> on page 401. 

The First Matter <note>original: "prima Materia"</note> is said to first become alive through the mixing of the two seeds of man and woman. There are said to be no more than six colors by which one can guide oneself; alongside this, the Mosaic history of Creation <note>The Book of Genesis.</note> is interpreted entirely alchemically. The Great Serpent that seduced Eve is said to be the Water through which the solution occurs, or the Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius"</note> that "kills" the gold <note>In alchemy, "killing" or "mortification" refers to dissolving a solid metal into a liquid state or changing its outward appearance to reach its inner essence.</note> on page 429. Following this is the *Key to Chemical Philosophy* <note>original: "Clavis Philosophiæ Chemicæ"</note>, which provides many reminders on how to properly understand and undertake the operations. 

The thorough report on what the true Art contains and is capable of in the *Universal and Particular Way* <note>original: "in via Universali & Particulari"; the Universal way sought the Great Elixir for all metals, while the Particular way focused on specific transmutations.</note>, drawn together from all the philosophers, gives a brief idea of the whole work. The Matter of the Stone <note>original: "Materia Lapidis"</note> is the same here in both Universal and Particular works, except that the Universal works are more subtle and require more effort and time than the Particular ones. What "Virgin’s Milk" <note>original: "Lac Virginis"</note>, "Sulfur of Nature" <note>original: "Sulphur Naturæ"</note>, and the "Separation of the Elements" <note>original: "Separatio Elementorum"</note> are is explained in the Lullian manner <note>Referring to the complex system of Ramon Llull (c. 1232–1316).</note>. 

*The Garden of Riches* <note>original: "Hortus divitiarum"</note> on page 500 is divided into 20 chapters; the augmenting and fermenting of the Stone to White <note>for silver</note> or Red <note>for gold</note> can happen in many ways, but for preparation and purification, there is only a single way and a single labor. There follows another work of alchemy divided into 12 chapters, teaching how one should fix the Sublimated Mercury <term>☿rium</term> <note>To "fix" a substance meant to make a volatile material solid and resistant to heat.</note> and prepare the Tincture. The two Tinctures for White and Red, as well as the work of Mercury <term>☿rij</term> and the augmentation with the Mercury of the Moon <note>original: "Mercurio Lunæ"</note>, are attributed to Dr. Nicolaus Malß on page 550.

# Preface.

...but they seem to be somewhat unbelievable. The beautiful "particular pieces" <note>In alchemy, "particular" refers to processes that achieve a limited transmutation of specific metals, rather than the "universal" work of the Philosopher's Stone.</note> are various attempts <note>original: "Tentamina"</note> by laboratory workers regarding how they tried to improve the metals. The work of Dr. Schenck has instigated many to try something with cinnabar <note>A bright red mineral, mercury sulfide, which alchemists often used as a source for mercury.</note>, though with little profit.

In the fifth and final treatise of this *Golden Fleece* <note>original: "guldenen Vliesses"</note> are contained *The Treasure of the Philosophers*, the *Philosophical Vitriol*, the *Experiments of Raymond Lully*, and several other minor writings. The first is, as it were, a collection of the many sayings that the philosophers have expressed here and there in their books <margin>page 23.</margin> regarding the Philosopher’s Stone, which serve to confirm the work; just as the secret of the Philosopher’s Stone corresponds with Isaac Hollandus’s method of working with Saturn <note>The alchemical name for the metal lead.</note>. The preparation of the matter is mostly borrowed from Theophrastus <note>Theophrastus Paracelsus, the influential 16th-century Swiss physician and alchemist.</note>. The treatise *On the Vitriol of the Philosophers* <margin>Lully</margin> <note>original: "de Vitriolo Philosophorum"</note> contains more theory than practice. The thirty-four *Experiments of Lully* are of a far better kind, utility, and certainty. For although (as already mentioned above) this Raymond Lully is often held in low regard by Theophrastus and other inexperienced men—such as when they wish to cast doubt on the *History of Transmutation* <note>original: "Historiam Transmutationis"</note> performed by him for King Edward and Robert—others have nevertheless formed a far better opinion of him. 

The well-known Frenchman Jean d'Espagnet, who published the *Work on the Secret of Hermetic Philosophy* <note>original: "Arcanum Hermeticæ Philosophiæ opus"</note>, being a particularly experienced chemist, "was most devoted to Lully alone," as Olaus Borrichius testifies, "than whom no mortal had more faithfully examined Lully, because he asserted that the entire chemical science lay hidden in him alone, and therefore showed himself concerned with no other chemical writer." One could therefore regard this book of his *Experiments* as the most reliable contained in the entire work of the *Golden Fleece*. Lully himself, in his treatise *On the Quintessence* <note>original: "de Quinta Essentia"</note>, page 15, gives the report "that the book of Experiments is the principal one and the key to all the books he composed in this art." 

To be sure, an anonymous author recently published *Lully Reborn* <note>original: "Lullium Redivivum"</note>, in which he seeks to explain the prescribed operations through special remarks; however, the author himself doubts whether he has correctly hit the mark in all things. For whoever does not compare <note>original: "conferirt"</note> Lully's chemical writings together and make an extract of his obscure ways of speaking will hardly reach the goal. Perhaps the publisher of this work, seeing that there are enthusiasts for it, will also bring to print the remaining books, such as *On the Quintessence*, his *Magica*, *The Opener* <note>original: "Apertorium"</note>, the *Letter of Abbreviation* <note>original: "Epistolam abbreviationis"</note>, and others. It would be too extensive here in the preface to undertake even a brief summary of all the experiments; the actual investigation will provide everyone with the necessary light. The booklet by Diony-

# Preface.

ij <note>A printer's signature mark indicating the second leaf of the gathering.</note> The work of **Zachary of France** <note>original: "Zachariæ Galli"; referring to Denis Zachaire (c. 1510–1556), a French alchemist famous for his autobiographical account of the hardships of the "Golden Art."</note> is well worth reading for the purpose of avoiding the errors that have crept into this Art. How he was murdered by his wife and servant is well known. The dispute and the dialogue of **Gold** and <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "☿ rij" (Mercurii)</note> against the **Philosopher’s Stone** is an ancient war that only experience must end. The "Particular Works" of **Korndorffer** <note>referring to Bartholomaeus Korndorffer, a 16th-century alchemist</note> serve as further explanation of the previously mentioned artistic feats by the same author. At the end of this treatise, the *Mirror of Philosophy* is added, in which one may see, through figures, images, and clear descriptions, the true nature of the **Golden Art**, and thus be better able to guard oneself against all deceptions. The gracious reader will therefore grasp the contents of the entire work in the briefest manner from this, and we do not doubt that a good sense of satisfaction will follow from so many heaped-up instructions and provided explanations.

It remains only to remind the reader that the person who handled the correction and edition of this work showed himself almost too scrupulous in retaining the old words and style of writing found in the first edition—such as where *Centilon*, *Gentilhuomo* <note>Italian: "Gentleman"</note>, *Singerey*, *Signoria* <note>Italian: "Lordship" or "Government"</note>, etc., are intended—while even the grammatical **barbarisms** and **solecisms** <note>Terms used to describe non-standard or "incorrect" linguistic forms, often used by scholars to mock the unrefined Latin of earlier alchemists.</note> were preserved. The distinction between the letters **v.** and **u.** will likewise cause no confusion, because the words written with a "closed v" in the first edition are here expressed throughout with an "open u."

Furthermore, not all the treatises were printed in one place (as it says on the title page); rather, volumes 1, 2, and 3 (as mentioned above) were printed at **Rorschach**. The fourth was published at **Basel** by **Janum Exertier** <note>Jean Exertier, a 17th-century printer</note> in the year 1604. The fifth likewise came out at **Basel**, by **Jacobum Treuw** <note>Jakob Treuw, a 17th-century printer</note> in the year 1604. May the lover of this **Golden Art** fare well, and let him always keep recommended to himself the rule of Holy Scripture from **1 Thessalonians 5:21**:

> ->Test all things, and hold fast<-
> ->that which is good.<-

# Treatise

# Travels
->Of the highly famous<-
# Master Salomon Trismosini /
->together with three powerful tinctures.<-

When I was a young journeyman, I came to a miner named Flocker, who was also an <term>alchemical artist</term> <note>In this context, an "artist" refers to a skilled practitioner of the chemical arts.</note>, but he kept all his affairs hidden; I could obtain nothing from him. He had a piece with common Lead <note>The symbol ♄ represents Saturn, the alchemical name for lead.</note> and a special <term>sulfur</term> <note>original: "Sulphur oder Schweffel"</note> added to it, and he sealed the lead for so long until it became fixed and fluid, later like a wax. Of this prepared lead he took 20 <term>Loth</term> <note>A traditional German unit of weight; 20 Loth is approximately 300 grams.</note> and 1 <term>Mark</term> <note>A unit of weight for precious metals; 1 Mark is approximately 234 grams.</note> of fine silver that contained no gold; he let both flow together for half a day, after which he separated the silver by casting, and it became half gold. My heart was deeply grieved that I should not possess the art, and I thought I would ask him for it, but it was denied me. Not long after, he perished in a mine, and no one could find anything of his art. Because I had seen this truth myself with this miner, I set out in the year 1473 <note>original: "Anno, etc. M. CCCC. LXXIII."</note> and traveled here and there; wherever I heard of an artist, I was diligent to reach him, and I spent a year and a half in these travels, and I learned all kinds of arts from <term>Alchemy</term>, which did not yield much; yet I saw the truth in several <term>particulars</term> <note>The "Particular" path in alchemy refers to specific chemical recipes for refining metals or creating medicine, as opposed to the "Universal" work of the Philosophers' Stone.</note> and spent 200 florins <note>original: "fl."</note> and yet thought not to give up.

<header>Treatise and Travels /</header>

I intended and was diligent to raise travel funds among my friends, and I took my journey with a foreign man toward **Ljubljana** <note>original: "Labach"</note>, from there to **Milan**, and came into a monastery; there I served as an assistant and heard his lectures for nearly a year; afterward I wandered here and there throughout **Italy** <note>original: "Welschlandt," a historical German term for Italy or other Romance-speaking regions.</note> and came to an Italian merchant and a Jew who knew German; these made English tin look like the best fine silver; they sold much of it. I offered to serve them if it were agreeable to them: The Jew persuaded the merchant to take me on as a servant, and I had to tend the fire when they performed their art with the tin; I was industrious, and it pleased them well, and therefore they kept nothing hidden from me; thus I also learned the art, which involved poisonous substances, and stayed with them for fourteen weeks.

Afterward I traveled with the Jew to **Venice**, who sold about thirty-five pounds of the silver to a Turkish merchant; while he was bargaining with the merchant, I took about six **Loth** <note>A traditional unit of weight; 6 Loth is approximately 90 grams.</note> of the silver and went to a goldsmith who had two journeymen, one of whom knew **Latin**, and requested that he test the silver for me: Then he directed me across **St. Mark's Square** to an **assayer** <note>original: "Probierer," a professional who tests the purity of precious metals.</note>, who was very grand and wealthy; he had three German assaying journeymen who quickly put it to the test with very sharp <term>corrosive substances</term>, and afterward refined it on the **cupel** <note>original: "Test," a porous vessel used in the process of cupellation to separate precious metals from base metals.</note>, but it failed and held no proof at all; everything vanished in the fire. And they spoke harshly to me, asking where I had gotten the silver; I declared that I had had it tested for the very reason that I might see if it held up as good silver.

When I saw the fraud, I returned no more to the Jew and esteemed this art not at all anymore, thinking I might perhaps fall into misfortune with the Jew and the false silver; and afterward I came to a school there in **Venice** and begged that I might have food twice a day. Then the Rector had me directed to a hospital; there were more Germans in it, and they gave grand meals there, as it was founded for all sorts of nations and foreigners. The next day I went to **St. Mark's Square**; there an assaying journeyman from where I had previously had the silver tested came to me; he addressed me, asking if I had more of the silver. I said no, but I had the art of how the silver was made and would gladly share it with him. This pleased the assayer well, and he asked me if I could also perform laboratory work. I said yes, reasonably so. Then he said that if I wished, there was a nobleman <gloss>[GENTILHOMME or gentleman]</gloss> here who had much laboratory work done and had long desired to have a German laboratory assistant. This pleased me, and he led me straightway to the gentleman’s chief laboratory assistant, who was a German, with

named **Hans Tauler**; and I was happy, for he hired me immediately and gave me two crowns every week, plus food. Then he led me about six **Italian miles** <note>original: "Welsche Meyl"</note> from **Venice** to a large house belonging to the same gentleman, which he called **Pontilon**. In all the days of my life, I have never seen such laboratory work—concerning all kinds of specific **tinctures** <term>Substances believed to have the power to change or "color" base metals into gold.</term> and medicines—as in this place. Everything one could imagine was in stock there; and every lab worker (of whom there were nine) had his own room, and they all had their own cook. There, the head chemist gave me a task to handle, which had been sent to the **Centilon** <note>Likely the name or title of the wealthy patron and master of the estate.</note> four days prior; it was a **solidification of Mercury** <note>original Latin: "coagulatio Mercurii." The process of turning liquid quicksilver into a solid state.</note>. The head chemist mixed all the powders for me so that I would not recognize them, and I had to work through this task; it was finished or completed in two days. I was diligent, and this **partial work** <term>original: "Particular," a specific alchemical procedure that achieves a result, but not the "Great Work" of the Philosopher's Stone.</term> turned out well for me. When the solidified substance was separated into nine **Loth** <note>A traditional unit of weight; 9 Loth is roughly 135 grams.</note>, three Loth of the best gold came out of it. That was my first success and stroke of luck. The head chemist immediately reported this to the Centilon, who came out to see me unexpectedly. He spoke to me in **Latin** and called me **Fortunatus** <note>Latin: "the lucky" or "blessed one."</note>. He was not perfect in his Latin, and he patted me on the shoulder; I did not understand him well as he spoke in a corrupted manner. He presented me with 29 crowns. Only then was I bound, by body and life, in place of an oath, that I would tell no human of the art. In short, everything had to be kept secret, which was only fair. And I say that if someone—as I have seen myself—boasts of this art, even if they have hit upon the truth, the eternal justice of God will no longer allow such art to proceed for them. Therefore, keep your mouth shut; even if you possess the highest tincture, give from it to the poor.

I saw that I could witness all kinds of arts with this Centilon, as the head chemist was very loyal to me; he put all kinds of arts into my hands and mentioned to me besides that his gracious master spent 30,000 crowns a year on such arts. He paid for all kinds of books in cash, whatever was brought to him in all languages, and gave great rewards besides. As I myself truly saw, a certain **Sarlamethon** brought a **tincture** in the **Greek language** from other lands, for which 6,000 crowns were given to him in cash. The Centilon also had it translated into German immediately and gave it to me to work on. I worked it out in fifty-five weeks; with it, I transmuted three metals—**Copper**, **Tin**, and **Silver** <note>original symbols: ♀ (Venus/Copper), ♃ (Jupiter/Tin), and Luna (Moon/Silver).</note>—in great quantity, all into the best gold. And this, above all else, was kept hidden from others.

### Treatise and Travels

The **Centilon** became so magnificent and powerful / and just as they "marry" the sea every year, and the entire **Signoria** <note>The governing body of the Republic of Venice.</note> is led out onto the water to throw a golden ring set with precious stones into the sea <note>This refers to the *Sposalizio del Mare* (Marriage of the Sea), a famous Venetian ceremony symbolizing maritime dominion.</note>. And this **Centilon** also presented himself with great splendor in his ships / then a storm of the sea arose / drowning many great lords / and so this great **Centilon** also went down to the bottom / whereupon his noble family ceased all the laboratory work / and all the laborers were diligently paid: yet the head chemist was retained.

So I came from **Venice** to an even better place / where **Cabalistic** and **Magical** books in the **Egyptian language** were entrusted to me / these I had translated into the **Greek language** / and from that into **Latin** / there I found and snatched up the entire treasure of the Egyptians / I also saw there / what the *subjectum* <note>original Latin: "subjectum." In alchemy, this refers to the "Subject of the Art," the raw material from which the Philosopher's Stone is made.</note> was / and the greatest pagan kings / used such **Tinctures** / and worked them themselves / namely King **Xophar**, King **Sunsfor**, King **Xogar**, King **Xopholat**, King **Iulaton**, King **Xoman**, and others / these all possessed a great treasure of the **Tincture** / and it is a thing to wonder at / that the eternal Godhead revealed such things to the heathens / but they remained silent about it. After I had spent a short time there / and saw what the foundation of this art was / I began to work on one of the best **Tinctures** (though they all spring, inexpressibly, from a single root) and as I reached the end / I found such a beautiful **Redness** / which cannot be compared to any scarlet / and such a treasure as is inexpressible / and which can be increased without end / Truly, after the **augmentation** <term>The process of increasing the power or quantity of the alchemical medicine (the Stone).</term> I transmuted <note>original: "thingiert," from the Latin *tingere*, to dye or transform.</note> one part into 1500 parts of **silver** into the finest gold. Before the augmentation, I turned one part into 1000 parts of **tin** / into the finest gold / likewise also **Copper** [♀], **Tin** [♃], and **Lead** / additionally, I took heated rods of **steel** or **iron** / threw the Tincture upon them / and they became the most malleable gold: I will not write now / after manifold augmentation / what amount of silver and other metals / I transmuted after the **multiplication** <term>A specific procedure used to exponentially increase the transmuting power of the Stone.</term> / at which I myself was terrified.

Whoever wishes to handle such great things / he should pray diligently / call upon and honor **God** / gladly give alms to the poor / and show himself with faithful help toward his neighbor / and abstain from evil vices / so shall great fortune appear visibly with these secrets / more than you will expect.

->Trissmosin.<-

# The book is named Trismosin / therein are found three powerful **Tinctures** / and other matters besides / as follows.

### Thus writes Salomon Trismosin of the red lion.

Many great secrets appear in all things in nature / which the highest **God** himself has ordered / so that even the children of men wonder / when such things are revealed to them. The great treasures lie within the earthen mountains / from which people must nourish themselves / and make their way through this world. For without the earth man cannot live / from which food and drink come / and we humans are not worthy of these gifts / which the merciful **God** sends us / Everything is misused / and there is only ingratitude toward the **Almighty God** / for which reason he does not allow many treasures to be revealed / and thus many arts remain hidden in this world because of our ingratitude / yet more is revealed to pious people than they might suppose / as I have often seen / that a poor man has many times come upon something great of **Gold** and **Silver**.

Now the **Red Lion** is the greatest treasure in this world, with which the children of men—for whom it was created—can perform great wonders, so that they may obtain health and wealth.

Truly, this **Lion** is an unspeakable essence of the **Tincture** <note>In alchemy, a "tincture" is a potent substance capable of "tinging" or transforming base metals into gold or silver.</note>, such that it transforms many thousands of parts in its augmentation [multiplication]. It transforms the imperfect metals—**Mercury**, **Tin**, **Lead**, **Silver** <note>original: "Luna"</note>, and others—at which I have had to stand in awe.

Whoever now wishes to work with it must be able to dissolve gold into its highest spirituality; then he will experience greater things than I can write. He must be a skillful artist who well understands the tinctures and their dissolutions, as well as the governance of the fire; otherwise, nothing can be accomplished.

## Now follows the water which is called Mercurial Water, in which the gold becomes
### the First Matter <note>original: "prima Materia," the primitive, formless base of all matter sought by alchemists.</note> and remains a virgin before and after the dissolution; that is the first work.

Take calcined alum and saltpeter, 8 units <note>original: "Loth," a historical German unit of weight, roughly 15 grams or half an ounce.</note> of each, and 4 units of common dried salt. Grind it all together into a fine powder. Afterward, take one and a half pounds of well-sublimated **mercury sublimate** <note>original: "☿rium suplimatum," a highly toxic compound of mercury and chlorine.</note> and one and a half pounds of the aforementioned powder of saltpeter and alum. Place it in an earthen sublimating vessel <note>original: "suplimatorium"</note>, well sealed with lute [sealing clay]. All of this having been finely ground, a knowledgeable lab worker should sublimate it until all the sublimate has risen. Sweep it off cleanly and with caution, so that the smoke does not enter you <note>A warning against inhaling toxic mercury vapors.</note>. Sublimate it again with fresh powder as mentioned above, with the same weight as stated. 

The lab worker should protect himself <note>original: "præseruirn"</note> and, while fasting, eat a fair-sized piece of fresh, unsalted butter. When he has eaten it, he should drink a strong wormwood wine <note>These were common early modern medical precautions intended to coat the stomach and "neutralize" the effects of toxic mineral fumes.</note>. Take this sublimate, finely ground, and put it into a glass flask. Pour over it a **spirit of wine** <note>original: "Spiritum vini," high-proof distilled alcohol.</note>. Place it in a water bath <note>original: "Balneum Mariæ," a gentle heating method using hot water.</note>. Distill it off very gently until half is gone, or to the half-part. Pour the spirit or brandy back onto it and distill it off again. Do this a third and fourth time, and so the sublimate will rise over with the brandy. If it does not, you must rot <note>original: "putrificieren," a process of slow digestion or fermentation.</note> the sublimate with fresh brandy. The brandy should always stand a finger's width over the material—

When the sublimate has risen into the receiving glass, take the entire **matter** <note>original: "Materia"</note> out of the glass or recipient, distill the whole substance over the helm <note>The top part of a still, also called an alembic head.</note>, and across for a second time; afterward rectify the risen sublimate into the four elements until it leaves no more residue, so that all is broken down and has become a hellish burning fire and water.

Now take this water in a Venetian glass <note>Venetian glass was prized by alchemists for its clarity and purity.</note>; upon it place Venetian paper seven-fold, and a helm on top; place it in clean ashes in very gentle heat, draw it over into the receiver, and where it still leaves a residue, draw it over once more through a seven-fold paper in a **Mary’s Bath** <term>Balneo Mariæ: a water bath used for gentle, indirect heating</term>, thus the water has entered into the four elements and is the true spiritual water; it should be well-preserved in Venetian glass and very well sealed at the top, for it is quite swift and volatile. — Now it is to be known that this **mercurial water** <term>Mercurialwasser: a corrosive liquid derived from mercury sublimate, intended to dissolve precious metals</term> does not dissolve gold in the way a common parting-water <note>original: "Scheidwasser," usually nitric acid used to separate silver and gold.</note> dissolves silver into the clouds [fumes], but rather it melts therein like butter or lard, and thus remains lying spiritually, yet not broken down into the four elements as the water itself is; for the true art requires nothing more than the **first matter** <term>primam materiam: the primitive, formless base of all matter sought by alchemists</term>.

## Thus dissolve the gold with this water
### as follows.

Take 6 units <note>original: "Loth," a historical German unit of weight, roughly 15 grams or half an ounce.</note> of the best Hungarian gold, called leaf-gold [found] at the goldbeaters', put it into a glass, bowl, or flask; pour the spiritual water upon it so that the water well covers it, seal the glass well at the top, place it in very gentle heat, so the **mercurial** <note>original: "☿rial," using the astrological symbol for the planet/element Mercury</note> water begins to work and dissolves the gold into the **first matter** <note>original: "prima materia"</note>, and leaves it lying like butter-fat; pour the water off from it, and know that this water is to be used again, for it remains a virgin without any blemish, becoming neither stronger nor weaker—that is now a wonder. Now take the **first matter** out of the glass, divide it in half; take one part in a glass, pour a proper **spirit of wine** <term>Spiritum vini: distilled alcohol or ethanol</term> upon it, let it **putrefy** <note>original: "putrificieren," to rot or decompose, a key stage in the alchemical process of transformation</note> for 15 days and nights in a **Mary’s bath**, so it becomes a blood-red **liquid** <note>original: "Liquor"</note>; that is the blood of the **Red Lion**. ### How to Tincture.

Take 1 part of this work / finely ground / and let 1000 parts of the best Hungarian **gold** <note>original: ☉, the astrological symbol for the Sun and the chemical symbol for gold.</note> flow strongly [melt] / then carry upon it in a paper the portion of the Tincture / let it remain in flux for three-quarters of an hour / so this one part transforms everything into a Tincture / Of this take 1 part / let 1000 parts of fine silver flow / and carry this upon it / that transforms it into the highest gold / which has never been seen / which is very soft under the hammer / almost like lead / and stable in all tests.
From this upper Tincture take 1 part / let 1000 parts of **mercury** <note>original: ☿ium</note> from the mountain flow in a clean **crucible** <term>crucible: a ceramic or graphite container used for melting metals at high temperatures</term> / made of earth / in the fire / when it begins to smoke / then carry the portion of the Tincture upon it / then it will become pure Tincture. # Now follows the Tincture of the Black Eagle, a great secret.

## The Black Eagle.

Take two pounds of raw <term>antimony</term> <note>original: STIBIO; a semi-metallic mineral used as a starting point for many alchemical processes</note> which the Philosophers call the Black Eagle / of the best quality you can obtain / from it make a beautiful red glass / as laboratory workers are accustomed to making / of which take 2 pounds / grind it very small for 4 hours / on a painter’s or grinding stone / and grind into it eight **lots** <note>A "Lot" was a unit of weight, roughly 15-16 grams.</note> of well-purified <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>original: Salmiac; ammonium chloride, used to assist in the dissolution of minerals</note> / put it all into a vial glass / in **horse manure** <note>original: Roßmist; used in alchemy as a source of gentle, consistent heat for "digestion" or slow fermentation</note> / that is steaming / for 10 days and nights / so the matter will resolve [dissolve] / and let it coagulate in a gentle warmth quite slowly / thereafter take the matter out of the glass / grind it small / put it again into a vial glass / and [pour] the following vinegar upon it / let stand 3 days and nights / then pour the vinegar into another glass or vessel away from it / pour more fresh vinegar on it / let it extract for 3 days and nights / do this with fresh vinegar / until it extracts nothing more.

## Here follows the hellish burning spirit / Sal ammoniac.

Take one pound of true *Sal ammoniac* <note>original: "Salmiar"; ammonium chloride, used in alchemy to create strong corrosive waters</note> / and one and a half pounds of common molten Salt / grind these two *species* <note>materials</note> small together / *sublimate* <note>to heat a solid until it becomes vapor and then solidifies again, a method of purification</note> them in a *sublimatorium* / and whatever rises up finely through the *sublimation* / sweep that off and grind it again / with an equal weight of common Salt / let it *sublimate* again / do this / until the *Sal ammoniac* manifests as an intangible spirit / grind this / and collect it on a smooth stone / put it in a glass / sprinkle it with *spirits of wine* <note>original: "Brandtenwein"; high-proof alcohol</note> / seal the glass well at the top / place it in a *water bath* <note>original: "Balneum Mariæ"</note> / until the spirit dissolves / strain this off / whatever has not turned to water / *putrefy* <note>original: "putrificier"; to break down through gentle, moist heat</note> it again / do this / until everything becomes water. When all is dissolved / then put the water into a tall *long-necked flask* / *distill* it in the *water bath* / until half is gone / pour the water back onto it / draw it off once more / then drive it with strong heat / until everything comes over the *helm* <note>the top part of the distilling apparatus</note> / then *rectify* it <note>purify by repeated distillation</note> / until it leaves no more *dregs* <note>original: "feces"</note> / thus is the hellish burning water prepared.

## A true and certain Cement / with the / Oil of the Black Eagle.

You shall take the glowing *Antimony* of the Black Eagle / one half-pound / cemented in white pieces / in *quicklime* <note>original: "ungelöschten Kalch"; calcium oxide, a caustic substance</note> / *layer upon layer* <note>original: "stratum super stratum"</note> / that is one layer after another / until it becomes red / inside and out / take this and grind it small / put it into a *long-necked flask* / pour *royal water* <note>original: "Aqua regis"; a powerful mixture of acids capable of dissolving gold</note> upon it / draw it off strongly / take this *Antimony* / put it into a wide glass / so that it lies flat / and pour the incombustible water or oil / of the Black Eagle upon it / so that it is well covered / stir it well together / leave it sealed at the top / to work for four days and nights / thus the incombustible oil makes the volatile Black Eagle *fixed* <note>stable and resistant to heat</note> and permanent in the fire / and this *Cement* may be used without ceasing.

Take a pale or white *Gold* <note>The symbol ☉ represents Gold; "white gold" likely refers to an alloy or gold not yet fully refined</note> / beat it thin / and with the *fixed Cement* / make *layer upon layer* in a crucible / cover it up / let it *cement* thus for four hours in a *circular fire* <note>original: "Zirkelsfeuer"; a furnace providing even, surrounding heat</note> / then take it out / and you will find the *Gold* at 28 degrees <note>an archaic measurement of extreme purity</note> / which is very high and this color remains through *lead* <note>original: "Bley"; a reference to the cupellation process where gold is tested by melting it with lead</note> / and all *tests* <note>original: "Examina"</note> / without any loss of the metal / which is a thing to be wondered at.

# The Tincture of King Julaton.

## Now follows the tincture of the great and mighty King Julaton, described by Master Trismosin.

This king, as an experienced philosopher, completed the following tincture and performed great wonders with it, for the wealth and health of mankind. This king has made a volatile woman out of a dead man, and the volatile woman has in turn made a dead man living; and the Lion has killed the volatile woman in his blood, and the two have become one. <note>This is an alchemical allegory: the "dead man" represents a solid, fixed metal—likely gold—and the "volatile woman" represents the spirit or mercury derived from it. The "Lion" usually refers to a strong acidic solvent like aqua regia.</note>

### This is the process as follows.

Take 12 parts of the best Arabian gold; dissolve it in the following water <note>Referring to the solvent described on the previous page</note>; draw off the water to the precipitate, and when it is well dried, grind into it half as much common brimstone <note>sulfur</note>, which has been subtly drawn from vitriol. Put the <term>☉</term> <note>symbol for Gold</note> and the sulfur into a crucible; let the sulfur burn away in a circular fire <note>original: "Zirckelferwr"; a fire that completely surrounds the vessel</note>. Do this with fresh sulfur for a third time, and thus the gold will be "opened" and appear a beautiful yellow-brown. Of this gold, take 8 parts into a cucurbit <note>a gourd-shaped distilling vessel</note>; pour the following water over it so it is well covered; let it be sealed with lute <note>an airtight clay sealant</note> for 21 days in a *Balneo Mariæ* <note>original: "water bath"</note> with gentle heat. Afterward, distill it and pour the water back onto it, drawing it off and pouring it back until the water remains upon it. Then take fresh water, pour it on, and begin to distill, but slowly; thus the gold will gradually rise over the neck of the vessel. In this way, a volatile woman has been made out of the dead man. Let it sit, then gently pour off the water and wash the calx <note>the fine powder remaining after heating</note> finely in a glass with spring water; do this several times, then dry it. This calx is volatile, like a <term>☿</term>rius <note>symbol for Mercury</note> drawn from a mountain. Take 8 loth <note>a unit of weight, roughly 1/2 ounce</note> of this volatile calx and 1 part of the gold kept from before; grind them both together on a stone; put them together into a crucible with a neck, sealed at the top. Set it in very gentle heat in ashes for 40 days and nights, and tend to it with the governance of the fire <note>original: "Regiment deß Fewers"; the careful regulation of heat levels</note>; thus the volatile will dissolve the inverted man, and the crucible will be blue for several days. Secondly, the crucible will show itself with a mixed redness, then blue again, after that black at the bottom and liver-colored, and afterward blue with red streaks and pale yellow, also red drops with gold streaks; there will also be seen gray

# Entrance of the Universal Tincture.

This aforementioned philosophical treatise speaks very clearly and openly of this Divine and over-rich Art; namely, since the chemical arts are a follower of Nature, that one should follow just and changeable Nature, and seek therein what God wishes to give as essential nature.

<margin>Three principles <note>original: "3 principia," likely referring to the alchemical triad of Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt.</note></margin>
Herein is explained the right and only way of which all philosophers have written in their own true philosophical understanding. For the origin, beginning, and matter of all things in the universal creation was a moist substance and watery nature, as is read in the Book of God’s Creation <note>The Book of Genesis.</note>. And although Moses first names the three principles as Heaven, Earth, and the Spirit of God, he immediately thereafter mentions the matter from which God created such Heaven, namely out of water; this God took for Himself and divided from one another into two parts or pieces, as shall be mentioned hereafter. All and every mineral in its kind is created out of an earthy, watery substance.

This mystery is an enemy of all metals, and when it is born anew to its first being—which our ancient students call *prime matter* <note>original: "primam materia," the fundamental, formless substance from which all things are made</note>—it brings with it the most ferocious animals: lions, crocodiles <note>original: "Crocatill"</note>, and fiery dragons, which only tear, swallow, and burn with and within themselves, making the imperfect entirely perfect with their fierce wrath. Yet, by its own power, the lion gives birth to an eagle which brings it food; thereafter, the crocodile swallows the lion, and the fiery dragon swallows the crocodile. Take from him his blood—the blood of the lion—and burn it together with the eagle with great power, and out of three, one shall become. Thus is this mystery described.

<margin>Red Sun <note>original: "Solem rot."</note><br/>red<br/>Philosophers' Mercury / Vitriol : Our Sun <note>Symbols: ☿ (Mercury), 🜔 (Vitriol or Salt), ☉ (Sun/Gold).</note></margin>
When the helm <term>helm: the upper part of a distilling apparatus (alembic) where vapors condense</term> begins to turn red, then strengthen the fire until it becomes as red as blood. After the redness has increased, pour the oil into a clean glass, well-stoppered; thus you have the true *oil of the philosophers* <note>original: "olium philosophorum"</note>, which shines by day and night in dark places. Know, however, that at the bottom of the glass, a beautiful white salt, like a crystal, will be found. Take it out, grind it into powder, put it into another clean glass, pour its own oil upon it, and imbibe <term>imbibe: to slowly add liquid to a dry substance so it is absorbed</term> it with the red blood; thus it will become a Red Stone, with which one can perform *projection* <term>projection: the final stage of alchemy where the Philosopher's Stone is cast upon base metals to transmute them into gold or silver</term> upon the metals.

Finally, the three principal colors appear in the Tincture: First, like a greenish lily <note>original: "grienlechte Gilg"</note> with gold streaks and a golden circle; thereafter the Tincture becomes fixed and incombustible, gray and white, with which one can transmute <note>original: "thingieren"</note> all fugitive <term>fugitive: metals like mercury that evaporate or change easily when heated</term> metals, one part to many 1000 parts; thereafter, with steady fire, the Tincture becomes scarlet red, and beyond red, and is a treasure above all treasures.

# Introduction to the Universal Tincture.
<meta>Catchword: Universal-</meta>

This aforementioned philosophical treatise speaks quite clearly and openly of this divine and most rich Art. Namely, since the Chemical Art is an imitator of Nature, one should follow true and mutable Nature, and seek therein what God and essential Nature wish to give.

<margin>// The 3 principles.</margin>
Herein is explained the right and only way of which all philosophers have written in their own true philosophical understanding. For the origin, beginning, and matter <note>original: "Materia"</note> of all things in the universal creation was a moist substance and watery nature, as is read in the Book of God's Creatures <note>This refers to the Book of Genesis.</note>. And although Moses first names the *three principles* <note>original: "tres principia"</note> as Heaven, Earth, and the Spirit of God, he soon after mentions the *Matter* from which God created such Heaven, namely from water; this God took for Himself and divided into two parts or pieces, as shall be mentioned hereafter. All and every mineral <note>original: "mineralia in genere"</note> are created from an earthly, watery substance.

This secret is an enemy of all metals, and when it is born anew into its first essence—which our ancient students call *first matter* <note>original: "primam materia"</note>—it brings with it the most fierce animals: lions, crocodiles <note>original: "Crocatill"</note>, and fiery dragons. These, with and within themselves, only tear apart, devour, and burn, making that which is imperfect entirely perfect with their fierce wrath. Yet the lion, by its own power, gives birth to an eagle that brings it food. Afterward, the crocodile devours the lion, and the fiery dragon the crocodile. Take from him his blood—the blood of the lion—and burn it together with the eagle with great force, and from the three, one is made. Thus is this secret described.

<margin>Only red gold <note>original "oph:" likely referring to Ophir, the biblical source of gold.</note> / <unclear>veß:</unclear> ☉ [Sun/Gold] red <unclear>astÿ</unclear></margin>
When the helm <note>The top part of a still or alembic.</note> begins to turn red, strengthen the fire until it becomes as red as blood. After the redness has increased, pour the oil into a clean, well-stoppered glass; thus you have the true *oil of the philosophers* <note>original: "olium philosophorum"</note>, which shines day and night in dark places. Know, however, that at the bottom of the glass, a beautiful white salt like crystal is found. Take it out, grind it to powder, put it into another clean glass, pour its own oil upon it, and saturate it <term>imbibe: the alchemical process of adding liquid to a dry substance until it is fully absorbed</term> with the red blood; so a red stone is formed, with which one can perform projection <term>projection: the final stage of the Great Work, where the Stone is cast onto molten base metal to transmute it into gold</term> upon the metals.

Finally, the three main colors appear in the tincture. First, like a greenish lily <note>original: "Gilg," an archaic term for a lily.</note> with golden streaks and a golden circle. Afterward, the tincture becomes fixed and incombustible, grey and white, with which one can tinge <term>tinge: to alchemically transform or "dye" the substance of a metal into a higher form</term> all volatile metals—one part to many thousands of parts. Afterward, with steady fire, the tincture becomes scarlet red and "beyond red" <note>An intense, deep red indicating the highest potency.</note>, and it is a treasure above all treasures.

Take two pounds of running Mercury <note>original: "☿"</note> as it is found in several places towards the sunrise [East] in the mountains / and twelve Loth <term>Loth: A historical German unit of weight, roughly 14.5 to 17.5 grams.</term> of the sulfur prepared above / and eight Loth of white calcined Giniton <note>original: "Giniton." Likely a proprietary or archaic name for refined nitre or saltpeter.</note> / Grind these two pieces small / let the sulfur flow with the Giniton / mixing the Mercury into it / and as much as it all weighs / grind it with half as much calcined Alum / and sublimate <term>Sublimate: To heat a substance so it becomes a vapor and then solidifies again, purifying it.</term> it in an earthen vessel / take this ascended Mercury again with half as much fresh Alum / sublimate it a second time / thereafter take again fourteen Loth of the sulfur mentioned above / and nine Loth of calcined Giniton mixed therein / but let the ascended Mercury stay in just as much fresh calcined Alum / just as before / and for the third time take twelve Loth of sulfur and eight Loth of calcined Giniton / mixing the Mercury therein and grinding it with half its weight of calcined Alum / sublimated / and then sublimate the sublimate again by itself in calcined Alum.

This work must be done with fresh sulfur / and calcined Giniton six times / then the Mercury <note>original: "Mercurij"</note> is prepared / and will be found for the last time in the sublimatory vessel / grind this small / put it in a urinal glass <term>Urinal glass: A round-bottomed glass vessel with a long neck, used in alchemy for digestion and distillation.</term> / well-sealed at the top with luting <term>Luting: A paste or cement used to seal alchemical apparatus airtight.</term>. Place it in horse dung <note>Horse dung was used as a natural, low-temperature incubator that provided steady warmth through decomposition.</note> for fourteen days and nights / and thus the Mercury <note>original: "☿rius"</note> becomes water. Distill this from the *Bain-Marie* <note>original: "Bad Mariæ" (Mary’s Bath). A method of gentle heating using a water bath.</note> / so the water rises over / pour that back into the glass / distill it again / do this by drawing it up and down four times or more / thus this Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius"</note> enters into the four elements / and becomes Mercury no longer / and is *by itself* <note>original: "per se"</note>, a pure, hellish, fiery water / *invisible* <note>original: "inuisibile"</note>. And this water shall be guarded in the best way / otherwise it immediately
->vanishes / for it is destroyed<-
->into the four elements.<-

->The Universal Tincture / of Master Hieronymus Crinot.<-

## Now the gold ☉ is purified, dissolved with the prepared key into a spiritual essence, and also separated and coagulated.

Take the purified gold and place it in a urinal glass <note>A flask with a long neck, shaped like a vessel used for medical examinations of urine.</note> with a long neck; pour the mercurial water [the "key" prepared previously] over it so that it covers it significantly. Seal the glass with lute <note>A clay-based sealant used to make glass vessels airtight.</note> and place it in very gentle heat, in a *Balneum Mariæ* <note>original: "Balneum Mariæ." A water bath or double boiler used for gentle, consistent heating.</note>, so that only the steam reaches it. Leave it for three days and nights, and thus the gold ☉ will become spiritual and volatile because of the water. Pour the water off carefully. Take the spiritual gold in the well-sealed glass and place it in cleanly swept ashes, setting it as deep as the matter can be seen. These ashes should lie in a very thin earthenware vessel, and under the vessel place a lamp <note>original: "Ampel." An oil lamp used here as a steady heat source for "digestion."</note> with six thick twine threads burning in oil. This shall stand for thirty days and nights in such warmth.

Afterward, one should make a wick of eight thick twine threads and keep it again for thirty days in steady warmth. Thereafter, use ten thick twine threads for thirty days; then take twenty thick threads in the lamp and let it stand for fifteen days and nights. Thus the spiritual gold will again become fixed and fire-resistant. In this way, it is coagulated once more into fixity. However, it is no longer a material gold ☉ as it was before, which can be reduced back into a physical body; rather, it is a Philosophical Gold. Of this, the masters say: our gold is not material, but an indestructible gold which penetrates all imperfect bodies.

## Now the dividing occurs, and thereafter the viscosifying.

Take the gold that has been made fixed and divide it into two equal parts. Keep one part. Grind the other part small and put it into a simple glass. Pour the aforementioned mercurial water over it so that it is slightly covered. Place it in a *Balneum Mariæ* <note>original: "Balneo Mariæ." A water bath.</note> for three days and nights. In this way, this part will all become spiritual and volatile again. This is called "viscosifying" <note>Making the substance thick or viscous, a stage in the transmutation process.</note> and being led into the *primam materiam* <note>original: "primam materiam." The "first matter"—the raw, undifferentiated base of all substances in alchemy.</note>. This second solution, performed after the first fixing, is the true *prima materia*. Herein lies the greatest *Arcanum* <term>Arcanum: A deep secret or a powerful alchemical mystery; the inner essence of a substance.</term> of the tincture. He is wrong who calls the first dissolution the *prima materia*; for the first is only a dissolved spiritual body that has been made fixed and rightly stable again through the fire.
