->The Universal Tincture / of Master Hieronymus Crinot.<-

## Now follows the final work / and it is precipitated into a stone.

Now take the primary matter <term>prima materia: the fundamental, raw starting material of the alchemical Great Work</term>, which you have made viscous with the mercurial water <note>original: "Mercurialwasser"</note>; pour the mercury <note>symbol: ☿</note> water off gently and dry this prepared matter. Rub it into the other part that you kept back. Place it in a urinal glass <note>A flask with a long neck, used here for observation</note> with a long neck; seal it and let it be fixed in ashes. Use a wick made of seven thick twine threads in an oil lamp <note>original: "Oelampel"</note> for twenty-one days and nights, and so the work will turn black <note>The stage of *nigredo*, or putrefaction</note>. Afterward, make a wick of ten threads and let it stand for fifteen days and nights, and it will become green and yellow in color. After that, for ten days with twelve threads, and it will become white in color; then the work is perfectly fixed, fire-resistant, and righteous. Now let the work stand with great fire until it becomes scarlet red; then the tincture is prepared, precipitated, and quite fluid and penetrating.

Thus the true "universal" is prepared and perfect, capable of tingeing <term>tingieren: the alchemical act of transmuting a substance by "coloring" it with the tincture</term> many thousands of parts when it is resolved again. There follows how one should tinge with it, whereby the great treasure manifests itself inexpressibly with great power. 

From this tincture, take much or little according to your opportunity. Let 1,000 parts of the best fine gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> flow in a crucible—there should be no other metal present—and cast the single part of the tincture upon it while in flux. This transforms the gold into pure tincture. Of this [newly multiplied] tincture, take 1 part and let 1,000 parts of fine silver flow; cast the tincture upon it, and it will become the best gold. Likewise with mercury <note>original: "Mercurio"</note>, tin, or lead. For iron, make it red-hot, like a rounded bar; for 1,000 parts of iron, cast two parts of the tincture upon it while it glows, then thrust it back into the fire; thus it becomes the best gold <note>symbol: ☉</note>, standing firm in all tests.

I have never seen a tincture described so clearly as this one, in which nothing is lacking. I have also worked one out with God's help; I completed it with great effort because I did not previously know the degrees of fire <term>gradus ignis: the specific intensities of heat required at different stages of the process</term>, which are all otherwise contained in this tincture. Not all philosophers have intended as faithfully as this Crinot. They kept it strictly hidden from the evil and base world, lest it should fall to the lot of some godless person, and they considered it rightly with a zeal—for the highest God does not will that we should all be rich.

### TO THE READER.

The following three augmentations have been placed here so that the old writing is still preserved, and Biltdorff provides testimony for Crinot in this Universal process.

# Three Augmentations
### from
# The Manuscript of Mr. Georg Biltdorff /
## who was an Abbot at St. Maurin.
### 

I worked on these following augmentations in my youth and tested myself with them; almost all of them succeeded well for me. The dissolution of the metals, such as gold and silver, does not fail in their spiritualization <note>original: "Geistligkeit"—the alchemical process of converting a solid metal into a "spirit" or volatile essence</note>. And I say these augmentations yield <term>tinctures: concentrated substances capable of transmuting base metals into gold or silver</term> when they proceed through their resolution <note>dissolving the solid back into a liquid state</note>. Whoever seeks differently in the <term>chemical art: alchemy</term> and does not remain with the spiritual dissolution, he errs completely. Therein lies the foundation; and it requires time for <term>fixity: the state where a substance becomes stable and no longer evaporates when heated</term> until, through its cooking, it becomes resistant to fire. After that, there is nothing more to be ruined, except that one must add its required portion <note>the "food" or additional metal to be transformed</note> and let it cook further; thus the treasure multiplies without ceasing. Whether it is started with Sol <note>original symbol: ☉, representing gold</note> or <term>Luna: silver</term>, nature acts with great power, which no man can fully conceive. Our bodies will not rise again unless they rot in the earth, much less could they pass through closed doors in an instant <note>An allusion to the resurrected body of Christ; the alchemist argues that metals must also "die" and "rot" before they can take on a "spiritual" form that can penetrate other matter</note>. So too, where the fixed metals do not <term>putrefy: undergo the process of rot and decay to allow for rebirth</term> and become spiritualized, there is no hope that they should penetrate through other metals.

And no imperfect body that is not fixed and produces smoke <note>fumes or vapors released during heating</note>—such as lead, tin, or copper—even if they are putrefied and made alive, they still do not penetrate like Sol and silver. These latter are perfect metals, pure in their essence, and otherwise permanent in earthly fire, remaining stable without the loss of their substance.

## The first augmentation is to be made thus.

Take one pound of common salt; melt it strongly in a sturdy earthenware vessel so that it flows; pour this onto a clean stone; melt it a second time and pour it; then crush it small. Put it into a pig's bladder, tie it shut, and hang it in cold water; thus in a few hours it will turn to water. Or, lay it upon a large, hollowed-out radish and place it in a damp spot; or else, lay it while hot upon a cold, smooth stone in a cellar. Take this salt-water into a *crucible* and *distill* it strongly over in a *water bath* <note>original: *Balneo Mariæ*—the 'bath of Mary,' a vessel of boiling water used to provide gentle, even heat</note>; pour it back into the *crucible* and *distill* it over once more; then it is ready.

Put this water into a glass [vessel]. Take two pounds of saltpeter in a sturdy earthen jar, and also twelve <term>Loth: a historical German unit of weight, roughly 15 grams or half an ounce</term> of pure sand from a flowing stream, mixed into the saltpeter. Burn this into the salt-water over a large coal fire for six hours; thus the water is prepared.

Take thirteen Loth of fine silver; granulate it into small pieces and put it into a *crucible*. Pour the water over it so that it is well covered; let it stand in gentle warmth for a time, until the water has torn the silver into a <term>calx: a metal reduced to a fine powder through heating or chemical action</term> and ground it down. Then pour off the water; dry the calx and do not wash it. Divide it into two parts. Take one part in a *crucible* and pour the fresh salt-water over it so it is well covered; place it in the *water bath* and draw [distill] it off and pour it back seven times. Then pour fresh water onto it, or renew the old water, drawing it off and back again, and pouring the water back on; thus the silver will rise over the <term>alembic: the 'helm' or cap of a distilling apparatus</term> with the water, and it has become spiritualized <note>original: *geistlich*—rendered into a volatile, vaporous state</note>. To this, add a little clean, warm water; then the spiritual silver will settle in the glass within a few hours. Afterward, pour off the water gently, and take clean water to wash <note>original: *abluiers*—from the Latin *abluere*, to rinse or purify with water</note> it once more, and dry it. As for the other part [of the silver] which is not spiritualized, pour [the water] off completely and dry it.

Now take six Loth of the spiritualized silver and one Loth of the other; rub both together on a smooth stone. Put it into a *crucible* that is flat and sealed <note>original: *perlutiert*—closed with 'lute,' a specialized airtight sealant made of clay, dung, or glass</note> at the top. Set it in ashes with very gentle warmth, like the sun shining during the dog days <note>the hottest weeks of summer</note>. Let it stand thus for twenty-four days and nights, and take good care that it does not rise during these first twenty-four days; then let it stand for another twenty-one days until it turns a brown color; thus it is prepared and <term>fixed: rendered stable and no longer subject to evaporation by fire</term>.

Then grind it small, and add to it half as much of the volatile silver; this the philosophers call the *mercury of the body* <note>original: *☿rium corporis*—Mercurium corporis, the essential liquid essence of the metal</note>, which is made just as reported above.

## Another Augmentation for Gold.

I, Georg Billdorff, received this augmentation in my youth from a bishop, a pious Catholic gentleman. I was his <term>famulus: a scholar's or cleric's personal assistant and live-in student</term>, and he trusted me greatly. He had many poor relatives, but he gave nothing from the bishopric to any of them; he did not even allow a soup to be served when a friend came to him.

But he possessed this augmentation and increased it so that every month he reduced <note>transmuted into solid metal</note> 1,000 ducats. This money he shared every six weeks among his poor relatives and also among the poor people. I, however, had to tend to this augmentation for him daily, and this bishop would sometimes talk with me at length, saying: "If someone had a treasure and hid it from the poor, he would have to do penance for a long time in the hereafter." And when he was about to die, a day before, he commanded me to bring him a small book from his cabinet; that was this augmentation. He ordered me to work it, to share it with the poor, and also to leave it behind me <note>to pass the knowledge on to future generations</note>; I promised him this.

Take a strong distilled spirit <note>original: *Brantenwein*—aqua vitae or brandy</note>, like the one the monks of Mesue <note>likely referring to the pharmaceutical school of Johannes Mesue</note> make, which they produce from the best wine lees and which contains no water. Take one pound of this, and eight <term>Loth: a historical German unit of weight, roughly 15 grams or half an ounce</term> of the best white-burnt <term>tartar: potassium bitartrate, a salty crust formed during wine fermentation</term>. Put this into a *crucible* and pour the spirit over it. Over the *crucible*, place a very fine, thin paper, three layers thick, and *distill* the spirit through the paper; thus the best part passes over and is sharp. Take the remaining tartar and calcine <note>heat to a high temperature to reduce to powder</note> it very well in a new earthenware vessel. Pour warm water over it so that the salt dissolves; let that [run] through a woolen bag...

Repeat this with the mercury of the body as before, and you will have a perpetual augmentation; you can increase it into many parts.

...into a running Mercury of Saturn <note>original symbol: ☿ ♄; "running" refers to the liquid state of quicksilver</note>, this essence—that is, a Mercurial Mercury of Saturn, though produced from an imperfect body <note>referring to lead, which alchemists considered an "unripe" or imperfect version of gold</note>.

Take 7 *Loth* <note>about 110 grams</note> of this running Mercury of Saturn and 1 *Loth* of finely granulated gold; put them together in a crucible. Pour the prepared spirit of wine <note>original: *Brantenwein*—distilled alcohol</note> over it as mentioned above and let it dissolve. Allow the spirit of wine to evaporate away <note>original: *abrauchen*—literally "to smoke off"</note> until it becomes a calx <note>a fine, dry powder produced by heating or chemical action</note>. This powder should be well-washed <note>original: *außgesüßt*—rinsed until all salts are removed</note> and dried, then placed in a crucible and set in ashes, just as was done with the gold. Let it stand for four weeks, following the proper regulation of the fire. Then divide it into two equal parts; into one part, rub a third as much of the Mercury of Saturn. Let it stand for three weeks with a regulated fire, then augment it again in the same way, and so on and so forth.

Now, for your sustenance <note>meaning for your practical use or profit</note>, take a third part of this gold augmentation. Let this melt with a flux <note>a substance added to help the metal flow</note> and refine it through lead <note>a process called cupellation used to purify precious metals</note>. It will then be the finest gold, stable in all tests, without any loss of its substance.

And whatever amount you have taken from the augmentation, rub that same amount of the Mercury of Saturn back into it; however, let it be fixed <note>rendered solid and non-volatile through heat</note> for three weeks before you take from it again. And I tell you: you can make a complete Tincture <note>the ultimate alchemical medicine or "Philosopher's Stone" capable of mass transmutation</note> out of these augmentations, provided you rightly understand how to dissolve its substance, upon which most of this work depends.

You can also make running Mercury of Saturn from tin and copper, and apply it to gold or silver just as well as any other running Mercury of Saturn. And even though these are not from fixed bodies <note>meaning they come from "imperfect" base metals</note>, they nonetheless purify themselves when combined with the pure bodies <note>gold and silver</note> so that Tinctures are produced from them, which can accomplish more than many would believe.

In the year 1510, a rather elderly man came to me and requested a bowl of soup at the monastery as a traveler. After he had eaten the soup, he asked for me, the Abbot, wishing to speak with me. I ordered him to be brought to me and asked what his desire was. He thanked me for the monastery meal and presented me with about three pounds of mercury ore <note>original: ☿ Ertz—likely cinnabar</note> as it grows in the mountains. He said he had found this mine in "Hysterlandt" <note>possibly a reference to Istria, or more generally "the back country"</note> and that it was nothing but pure mercury—or, as he called it, an imperfect running metal that the Sun <note>the celestial heat believed to "ripen" metals in the earth</note> had not yet properly "cooked"; otherwise, he said, it would have become silver. And he knew very well how to separate it from the red earth, and it became a beautiful, running Mercury <note>original: ☿</note>.

<header>Three Augmentations / from the manuscript of Mr. Georg Biltorff.</header>

I asked him, however, what he did with it and for what purpose it was used; he said that with silver and gold one could make it hard, so that it would also become gold or silver. I desired to know this and would not let him leave, and I kept him in my chambers for four days and spoke much with him. He showed me a piece of gold and mentioned that a mountain dwarf <note>original: *Bergzwerglin*—in German folklore, these were supernatural beings or spirits thought to dwell in mines and possess secret knowledge of metals and ores</note> had taught him this, and that it was good gold. I tested it; it passed the test well. I pressed him on whether he would not like to try his art there with me; he was willing and said so gladly. He took one pound of this Mercury <term>original symbol: ☿; also known as quicksilver</term> in a crucible, over which he poured about 8 *Loth* <note>a *Loth* is a historical unit of weight, roughly 15 grams or half an ounce</note> of strong wine vinegar, and he added a good handful of salt, and let the Mercury boil with the vinegar for three hours. Afterward, he pressed it through a four-fold linen cloth and boiled it again for two hours, and pressed it through once more, and said that it was thus purified.

Thereafter, he took a very sharp wine vinegar, which he strained through a four-fold woolen cloth until it was quite pure. Of this, he took half a pound and poured it into a cucurbit <note>a gourd-shaped glass vessel used in distillation</note>, and he took an earthen jar into which he put two pounds of saltpeter, half a pound of salt, and half a pound of coarse sand from a stony, flowing stream—all mixed together. He placed the jar in a charcoal fire <note>original: *Kolfeyr*—likely a specialized furnace or heap of glowing coals</note> and burned the saltpeter and salt in the vinegar, first gently and then strongly, for ten good hours. Thus the vinegar was prepared; and he said that if the vinegar would not dissolve the Mercury, one must take all the more saltpeter.

Now he took two *Loth* of fine gold, which he granulated into small pieces over a delicate little broom-twig, and put this gold into a crucible. He dissolved 6 *Loth* of the purified Mercury in 8 *Loth* of the vinegar and poured it onto the gold, setting it in gentle heat for an hour so that the gold dissolved. Afterward, he distilled the vinegar strongly away from it; he took the crucible and set it in clean ashes for 15 days with gentle heat, and then 8 days stronger, until he had spent thirty days on it. Thus the Sun <term>original symbol: ☉; the alchemical sign for gold</term>—as he said—had also turned the Mercury into gold. He took the work and an equal weight of small-grained lead, mixed them together, and let them flow strongly for one good hour in an earthen cupel <note>original: *Schelltegel*—a porous vessel used in the refining process to separate precious metals from base metals</note>. Afterward, he placed this on ashes, packed tightly together, and covered it closely with a charcoal fire. Then it began to smoke until it stopped of its own accord. There the gold all remained lying, very beautiful, and all the Mercury had become Gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note> except for one *Loth*. And the Gold was very good; I tested it myself and also had it tested; it stood up to the greatest and highest tests.

# Preface to the Egyptian Royal Tincture.

This Tincture was written by the hand of the great philosopher Hieronymus Crinot / using a secret alphabet. It is well-suited for translation into English <note>original: *verteutschen* (to translate into German); the author is noting the accessibility of the text once decoded</note> / though he did not write his German very well. This dissolution with this Tincture has a pleasant flavor / is healthy to work with / and the work is accomplished entirely with its own essence and tools / nothing foreign is added to it / except its own <term>Viscosa <note>original: *Viscosa*—a sticky or glutinous substance; in alchemy, this refers to the "mercurial glue" that binds the elements together</note></term> / once the <term>Solution <note>original: *Solution*—the process of turning a solid substance into a liquid state, the first major step in the Great Work</note></term> has occurred / and this Tincture is prepared over nine weeks / This was known to the pagan kings / and others besides. However, such workers of the Tincture should not be vagabonds / bunglers, or <term>Grillenschmelzer <note>literally "cricket-melters"—a derogatory term used for fraudulent alchemists or "puffers" who followed foolish whims (*Grillen*) rather than true natural philosophy</note></term> / who search within common sulfurs / doing everything in haste / working only to become rich quickly / wanting to spoil much gold <note>original symbol: ☉; the sun, representing Gold</note> / and when they do not achieve such a Tincture / they claim the true Art must be a lie / they turn great lords away from such a foundation which is certain / and deceive them of many thousands of guilders with their lying <term>Particularien <note>original: *Particularien*—specific, "shortcut" recipes that claimed to change only a small part of a metal, often used by frauds to trick patrons</note></term>. Water is dissolved and coagulated again; do this for the third time, then it is correct. Then pour the distilled wine over it and, as before, seal it six-fold with <term>chamois bladders <note>original: *Gempfen Blatern*—tough animal membranes used to create an airtight seal for high-pressure distillation</note></term>. Then pour the volatile mercury over them—just as it rose over with the burning water—and let the water cover it well. Afterward, place it in gentle heat; leave it in the ashes until it boils down, which happens in 3 weeks. In the final 8 days, make the fire stronger so that it becomes quite dry. Then grind it again and put it back in the cucurbit. Add some of your volatile mercurial water to moisten it, and let it stand for eight days. If it is dry again, you should moisten it once more with a little of the aforementioned water and let it stand for another eight days. The colors are visible signs: black, gray, a dark color, yellow, white, and afterward red and "beyond red." It achieves all these colors in nine weeks. If you thus bleach the work you have begun with the aforementioned mercurial water, the instrument is ready for stability.

This is now the Philosophical Gold. It must be dissolved with its burning mercurial water as prepared above; it will soon boil down again, and then the true Tincture is ready.

A swift worker must know how to dissolve this diligently; upon this depends the power to transmute all the metals, which are the gifts of God.

## And you shall perform the <term>tincture <note>original: *thingieren*—the alchemical process of applying a catalyst to a base metal to transform its substance</note></term> as follows.

You should know that this Tincture does not flow or melt on its own; it must be used for tincturing upon a perfect metal. With such a metal, it enters the <term>flux <note>original: *Fluß*—the state of being molten or liquid under heat</note></term> and becomes good Gold of a high and fine grade.

Take 20 parts of fine gold and let it melt. Into this, throw 3 parts of the aforementioned Tincture. Let it flow for a good while. Afterward, take 1 part of this molten mixture and throw it into the flux of 40 parts of good Gold. Let it flow for a while; this is now a "multiplied" Tincture. From this, take 1 part and apply it to 1,000 parts of fine silver, and it will become the best gold.

From the 40 parts mentioned above, take 1 part and let 500 parts of red copper melt. Apply the mixture to it and let it remain in the heat for a full hour; thus it becomes high-grade and good Gold without any loss of weight.

Take 1 part from the fortieth-part mixture and let 800 parts of <term>English Tin <note>Cornish tin was highly prized in alchemy for its purity and specific metallurgical properties</note></term> melt. Apply the mixture to it and let it flow for half an hour; thus it becomes good Gold. This Gold, when separated from other gold, is the best and most <term>malleable <note>original: *geschmeydig*—soft and easy to work, a sign of high-quality gold</note></term>.

You should know that this Tincture turns all volatile metals into the best metal, <term>gold <note>symbol: ☉</note></term>. I have described this secret Tincture just as I did when I returned from Egypt.

-> <note>original: *NITROGEL SINON PELGON SEM AMEN*—A ritualistic or coded phrase common in early modern alchemical texts, likely derived from corrupted Greek or Hebrew roots intended to seal the secret.</note> NITROGEL SINON PELGON SEM AMEN. <-

To tincture iron with this Tincture: have a <term>small rod <note>original: *Zaindel*—a small cast bar or ingot of metal</note></term> or bar of iron weighing half a pound forged round. Then let it be heated until it glows, and quench it many times in human urine. Afterward, let this iron glow intensely again, and while it is glowing, sprinkle a little of this Tincture upon it. Using only a little, it becomes red Gold. This, in turn, tinctures silver into a pale Gold.
-> Amen. <-

# THE BOOK SUFORETHON
->By Salomon Trismosin.<-

## In this book, the way to achieve long life for mankind in this world is found. A man can sustain himself for many hundreds of years, if it were not against God’s will, for the life of all men rests entirely in His Divine hands. As an example, the most powerful pagan King Xopholat refreshed his life for 300 years with the following Arcanum <note>original: *Arcano*—a secret or mysterious remedy, often alchemical in nature</note>.

All great lords—indeed, I say both the poor and the rich—who are able to prepare this great treasure for a long life, should prize this Arcanum above all other secrets. They should also keep it hidden for the sake of their own health, just as one keeps a hidden treasure in secret. Within it lies the living essence, through which all illnesses can be healed and the body is naturally preserved.

Beside this Suforethon, all apothecaries must hide away with their syrups, which only cause <term>putrefaction <note>original: *putredinem*—decay or rotting of the bodily fluids</note></term> and foulness in the blood. This Arcanum brings the foul blood into a state of <term>renovation <note>original: *renouation*—a total renewal or restoration of the body's systems</note></term>, so that the <term>radical moisture <note>original: *humor radicalis*—in medieval medicine, the vital fluid or "lamp oil" of life that exists in the body from birth and is consumed by heat as we age</note></term> is found to be as pure and fresh as that of a young child. Furthermore, it is so rectified—which is a great secret—that God the Lord has placed it in this Suforethon for the good of mankind.

I, Trismosin, have already made myself and other brave people new again with this secret. If one so desired (were it not against the eternal wisdom of God), he could sustain himself with this <term>Arcanum <note>original: *Arcano*</note></term> until Judgment Day. But a pious, God-fearing man who strives for heavenly treasures does not desire to live in this wretched world; even if we live for a long time, we have nonetheless spent our lives in toil and labor.

The pagan King Xopholat was an excellent warlord who placed himself at the head of his campaigns, defending his land and people with armed—

# Thus writes the great philosopher Crinot concerning the most powerful King Xopholat in Egypt,
## how he possessed the treasure of the Great Tincture.

This King was a very excellent and great lord who possessed the treasure of the Great Tincture and accomplished much good with it among both the poor and the rich; a powerful, victorious king. This Xopholat was an enemy of all sorcery and had many sorcerers burned. And he kept this <term>secret remedy <note>original: *Arcanum*</note></term> hidden as a great treasure so that no one could detect it, as everyone should do who possesses it, otherwise there will be little luck in it. There follows hereafter his Tincture, how he used it and had it prepared.

## The Tincture follows.

Take the sulfur from the mountains in which gold grows. Grind this fine, and refine it to a <term>fine sediment <note>original: *Schlicht*—a technical term for washed, finely ground ore</note></term> so that it becomes entirely pure. Dry this as best as possible and put it into a <term>cucurbit <note>original: *Cucurbitam*—a gourd-shaped glass vessel used for distillation</note></term>. Pour the following water upon it, so that it covers it considerably. Seal the glass with care; set it to putrefy in <term>horse manure <note>Used by early chemists as a source of gentle, consistent heat</note></term> for one month. After that, distill the water from it until it reaches an oily consistency. Pour fresh water upon it and let it stand in a <term>Bain-marie <note>original: *Bal. Mariæ*—a gentle water bath</note></term> for eight days and nights. Afterward, draw the wateriness off from it until it reaches an oily consistency. Then set the glass with the matter in a <term>charcoal fire <note>original: *Kolfewr*</note></term> <term>through the side <note>original: *per latus*—a method of distillation where the vessel's neck exits the side of the furnace</note></term>, into a <term>receiver <note>original: *Fürleg*</note></term>. Distill it gently at first, then more strongly, and a blood-red oil will rise over. Maintain the fire with constant heat until everything has come over. Then take the oil and rectify it through fresh glasses, as a skilled <term>laboratory worker <note>original: *Laborant*</note></term> well knows how to do. Now take some running, purified <term>mercury <note>original: *☿*</note></term>; put twelve <term>loth <note>A unit of weight roughly equal to 15 grams or half an ounce</note></term> into a good cucurbit glass. Upon this, pour the prepared oil, so that it covers it considerably,

Fixed / Air and Water are volatile and spiritual; an artist should note this. For this reason, all **salts of metals** and **elixirs** are melting and penetrating, because their innermost nature is dried out <note>literally "kiln-dried" or parched</note>. And where such **salts** <note>original: *Salia*</note> are transformed into **oil** and coagulated according to their nature, they tincture the imperfect metals more than many can imagine. Therefore, the entire secret lies in the **salts of the metals**, from which then come **Spirit, Body, and Soul** <note>original: *Spiritus, Corpus und Anima*</note>, yet inseparably; for this reason, the salts after solution are also called the **first matter** <note>original: *prima materia*</note> by the philosophers. I will now remain silent regarding the dissolution of metals and describe the greatest secret of **Vitriol from Hungary** <note>a high-quality sulfate mineral, often copper(II) sulfate, prized for its purity</note>, what a great tincture is hidden within it and how it is to be used.

### P R O C E S S <note>original: *PROCESSVS*</note>

Take 12 pounds of the very best **blue Hungarian Vitriol**; grind this very small; dissolve it in clear, pure water or distilled rainwater; let the dregs <note>original: *feces*—the solid impurities or sediment</note> sink. Thereafter, pour the water into a glazed bowl; place it in a brass basin which shall be full of pure sand. Set the basin upon a kettle that is full of warm water and placed over a fire; let the water in which the Vitriol is evaporate <note>original: *abrauchen oder euaporieren*</note> until a skin appears on top; then let it cool and let it stand for three days and nights; thus, in the cold, green-blue transparent **little stones** <note>crystals</note> will form.

Take these formed little stones, put them into a glass bowl or a large glazed vessel; make fire again under the kettle; let it boil until a skin appears on top again; let it cool again and let it crystallize again; let this happen **seven times**. Thereafter, take the Vitriol and put it into a warm room, as hot as the sun shines during the **dog days** <note>the hottest period of summer, late July to August</note>; thus the Vitriol, after the seven solutions, will turn into a **white powder** in the heat.

Now take this prepared Vitriol into a large **cucurbit** <note>a gourd-shaped glass flask</note> with a long neck, **sealed** <note>original: *perlutiert*—closed tightly with alchemical cement or "lute"</note> at the top; place the glass in an **ash-bath** <note>original: *Aschen Capellen*—a container of ashes used to provide gentle, even heat</note>; under it place a **lamp**, so that the heat is no greater than the sun shines in March; let it stand so long until it begins to turn **yellow**; and when it becomes entirely yellow and begins to turn **brownish-yellow**, then increase the fire in the lamp by one degree, and maintain it in such heat for ten days and nights; and watch whether it begins to turn **red**; then increase the fire in the lamp by another degree, and maintain the fire until it becomes entirely red and beyond red; and thus

## The Fourth Tincture.

Take one pound of <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>original: *Salmiar*—ammonium chloride</note> and one and a half pounds of <term>fused salt</term> <note>original: *geflossen Saltz*—salt that has been melted and solidified</note>, rubbed very finely together on a stone. Afterward, <term>sublimate</term> <note>to heat a solid until it becomes vapor and then solidifies again</note> it in the <term>aludel</term> <note>a pear-shaped pottery vessel used in sublimation</note>. Save whatever sublimates into a fine substance, take this risen sal ammoniac, and rub it again with fresh fused salt. Sublimate it once more in the aludel; do this until the <term>Spirit of Sal Ammoniac</term> <note>original: *Spiritus Salisarmoniaci*</note> becomes a delicate, intangible spirit. Collect this very diligently in a glass and sprinkle it with <term>spirit of wine</term> <note>original: *Spiritum vini*—distilled alcohol</note>. Set the glass in the steam of hot water to <term>dissolve</term> <note>original: *soluieren*</note> for four days and nights. What has dissolved, pour off gently into another glass and let it dissolve further, pouring it off again. However, what will not dissolve must be sublimated again with fresh salt; do this until all the sal ammoniac turns to water. Then take the dissolved water in a tall glass and distill it over again very gently. If it yields no "spirit," add a little spirit of wine to the water and set it in a <term>Bain-Marie</term> <note>original: *Bal. Mariae*—a gentle water bath</note> to <term>putrefy</term> <note>to break down or rot</note> for eight days. Afterward, distill it over again, and it will become a fiery spirit; <term>rectify</term> <note>purify by repeated distillation</note> this in clean glasses until no residue remains, but everything has become water and a fiery spirit. This spirit dissolves and penetrates all metals and minerals; they dissolve in it like sugar in water and never become metallic again. And when one dissolves <term>gold</term> <note>original: ☉</note> or silver in it, the <term>gold</term> no longer returns to a physical body, but remains a spiritual essence.

Take at least four <term>lots</term> <note>a historical weight, approximately 2 ounces or 60 grams</note> of finely filed <term>gold</term> <note>original: *Golt*</note>. Put it into a clean glass and pour this Spirit of Sal Ammoniac over it. Let it putrefy, well-sealed at the top, in a Bain-Marie for ten months. Then the <term>gold</term> <note>original: ☉</note> will become a black oil. Then slowly draw the spirit away from it, so the oil remains at the bottom. Pour all of this onto <term>coagulated mercury</term> <note>original: ☿ *coagulat*</note> that has been coagulated without metal or sulfur; let them coagulate together into a red powder. Take one part of this powder and project it onto 100 parts of purified, running <term>mercury</term> <note>original: ☿</note>; this turns it all into a tincture. You should keep this carefully in a boxwood box.

Of this tincture, take one part and take a steel rod hammered thin. Heat it until it glows, and sow one part of this tincture onto 50 parts of it; that results in a very high-quality gold. Likewise, let copper or tin—whichever you wish—flow, 1000 parts of each, and throw the tincture upon it. Every metal will truly become the best gold.

From that, take one part and project it onto 1000 parts of tin or silver. Let it flow strongly for three-quarters of an hour, then pour it out. You will then have the highest gold, passing all tests at over twenty-eight <term>degrees</term> <note>a measure of the gold's purity or "grade"</note>. ## And its process is as follows.

Take one pound of raw antimony and two <term>loth</term> <note>A historical German unit of weight, approximately 14.6 grams or half an ounce.</note> of common salt. Take it and weigh it, and rub into it an equal weight of white arsenic, and half as much common sulfur as the arsenic weighs. Put it all together into a glass, and pour onto it an <term>ammonium chloride water</term> <note>original: *Salmiarwasser*</note>, just as the common laboratory workers make it. Let it cover the material well. Place it in <term>horse manure</term> <note>A traditional method of providing gentle, steady heat through the natural fermentation of the manure.</note> for ten days and nights. Afterward, <term>coagulate</term> <note>To thicken a liquid into a solid or semi-solid state.</note> it in a sand bath until you find a sulfur that is red. Take this, crush it in a mortar, and put it into a large <term>flask</term> <note>original: *Kolbenglas*</note>. Take a very strong wine vinegar and pour it over the material so that it is well covered. Let it coagulate in the sand until it is like a thick pap. Then pour fresh vinegar onto it and let it boil down; do this a third time. Afterward, lay the flask <term>on its side</term> <note>original: *per latus*—distilling horizontally to allow heavier vapors to pass over.</note> and distill it with a fresh fire into a receiver. First do this gently, then increasingly stronger, and finally very strong, so that a blood-red oil rises over. Take the <term>phlegm</term> <note>The watery, inactive portion of a distillate.</note> from this in a <term>water bath</term> <note>original: *Bal. Mar.* (Balneum Mariae)—a vessel placed in boiling water to ensure even, limited heat.</note>; then it is ready.

Take eight loth of <term>mercury sublimate</term> <note>original: *☿ sublimati*—mercury(II) chloride.</note>, as they make it in Venice. Of this, take one part; let thirty parts of fine silver melt very strongly, and add the finely rubbed part of the stone to it. Let it remain for half an hour, pour it out, and refine it <term>through lead</term> <note>original: *per Saturnum*—Saturn is the alchemical symbol for lead, used here in the cupellation process to purify precious metals.</note>; that is white gold.

## The eighth tincture in the sequence.

Take sixteen <term>loth</term> <note>a historical unit of weight; sixteen loth is approximately eight ounces or half a pound.</note> of fine silver; granulate it very finely and put it into a good, durable glass. Pour twenty-four loth of <term>Aqua fortis</term> <note>original: *Aqua fort*, literally "strong water," referring to nitric acid.</note> over it. Let it dissolve into a "water of clouds" <note>a cloudy or milky solution</note>. Into this, add three loth of finely rubbed <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>ammonium chloride</note> and draw off the <term>Aqua fortis</term> in [hot] ashes until it thickens. Seal the top of the glass and place it in a <term>Bain-marie</term> with very gentle warmth for thirty-one days and nights. After that, pour a very sharp <term>spirit of wine</term> <note>original: *Spiritum vini*, high-proof distilled alcohol.</note> over it so that it well covers the <term>matter</term>, and begin to distill it gently in the <term>Bain-marie</term>. Pour the distilled brandy back onto it and distill it again, and once more pour <term>spirit of wine</term> over it and draw it off; finally, drive the heat strongly so that the silver rises together with the brandy over the <term>helm</term> <note>the top part of the distilling apparatus</note> of the glass. Let this sit for two days and nights, and the <term>viscous matter</term> <note>original: *Viscosa*</note> will settle at the bottom. Pour off the water from the top very carefully and dry the <term>viscous matter</term>. Divide this into two equal parts. Take one part in a glass and place it in ashes; let it <term>fix</term> <note>original: *figieren*; to make a substance stable so it no longer evaporates or changes when heated.</note> until it becomes entirely resistant to fire. Then take this and rub it very fine, and mix the other half-part into it. Place it again in a vial in ashes to <term>fix</term> and <term>coagulate</term>; after that, the tincture is ready.

# The Red Eagle
## By Salomon Trismosin /
### wherein wonders are to be performed in noble stones and metals.

I, Salomon Trismosin, cannot leave unmentioned that within <term>Felch</term> <note>an archaic or regional name for silver; original: *Felch*</note>, which the Germans call silver, a great mystery is hidden; its vapor is transformed into a spiritual water, which is compared to a red eagle. This you should understand in this way: when its innermost part is turned outward, it is then an eagle that tears apart other common animals and birds. This water does the same, and when it is turned into the red state, it accomplishes great things. 

I have seen an Egyptian who, with this <term>Arcanum</term> <note>a secret alchemical mystery or remedy; original: *Arcano*</note>, <term>tinged</term> <note>chemically transmuted or colored; original: *thingiert*</note> several common metals (which possess the density of gold) into the finest gold; he also performed many other things upon white precious stones so that they became unspeakably radiant. This red eagle soars so high above all metals, as I myself have experienced, that it even transforms the reddest gold into a pure, clear silver, which is then no longer regarded as gold. And even if one applied all <term>parting waters</term> <note>acid solutions used to refine or separate metals; original: *Gradirwasser*</note>, <term>cementation powders</term> <note>used in the dry refining of gold; original: *Ziment*</note>, and <term>gradations</term> <note>processes intended to improve the quality or color of a metal; original: *Gradationes*</note> to it, it can no longer be brought back to its red color.

## Crown Electrum.

Take 4 <term>Loth</term> <note>A historical German unit of weight, roughly 15 grams; original: *Loth*</note> of gold, filed as finely and as subtly as possible, and 3 Loth of common cinnabar that is very red and well-<term>sublimated</term> <note>purified by heating the substance into a vapor that then solidifies; original: *gesublimiert*</note>; grind these two together well, place them on a flat plate, and gently <term>reverberate</term> <note>to heat a substance in a furnace where the flame is reflected back onto the material; original: *referberier*</note> the cinnabar away from it, as a skilled worker knows well how to do. Do this with fresh cinnabar a second and third time. Afterward, take the reverberated gold in a flask—it should not be very tall—and pour **Royal Water** <note>A powerful mixture of acids capable of dissolving gold; original Latin: *Aqua regis*</note> upon it, which has previously been drawn from **Sublimated Mercury** <note>Mercury chloride, used here as a reagent; original Latin: *Mercurio Sublimato*</note>. Place the fixed substance into a clean glass, then pour the **Red Oil of the Eagle** (as named above) upon it, so that they <term>coagulate</term> together into a reddish-brown stone; and thus the **Electrum** is prepared.

And since one cannot always have this mountain **coagulated** <note>original: *coagulatum*; referring to the solidified form of the alchemical substance</note>, golden **magnesias** <note>original: *Magnesien*; in alchemy, magnesia refers to a mineral substance believed to contain the "seed" of metals, not modern magnesium</note> are found in many gold-bearing mountains, as the miners call them; within them is also the true **sulfur of nature** <note>original: *Sulphur naturæ*</note>. **T**ake eight loth of sulfur, two loth of <term>gold leaf</term> <note>original: *☉ fol. von Goltschlagern*; gold beaten into very thin sheets</note> from the gold-beaters, and fourteen loth of <term>mercury</term> <note>symbol: ☿</note>. Make an amalgam; prepare it as one makes common <term>cinnabar</term> <note>mercury sulfide, typically used as a red pigment</note>, and sublimate it until it becomes a cinnabar. Grind this cinnabar fine and put it into a <term>cucurbit</term> <note>a gourd-shaped glass vessel used in distillation</note>, well-sealed at the top. Place it in warm sand and let it fix for twelve days, ensuring that it does not smell or rise up. Take one and a half loth of this cinnabar and, in a crucible, drive four loth of <term>lead</term> <note>symbol: ♄</note> and four loth of fine <term>silver</term> <note>symbol: ☽</note>; while in flux, cast one and a half loth of the cinnabar upon it. Let it drive until the <term>lead</term> <note>symbol: ♄</note> disappears and no longer smokes; thus the <term>silver</term> <note>symbol: ☽</note> is good, and half the <term>lead</term> <note>symbol: ♄</note> has become <term>silver</term> <note>symbol: ☽</note>. Refine it as is written or mentioned in the previously cited chapter.

->The end of the book of Moratosan.<- <note>original: *Finis libri Moratosan*</note>

T I N C T V R E,

# The Nesolon
->by the short way<-
## By Salomon Trismosin

<image-desc>An ornate decorative initial 'I' begins the first paragraph, featuring intertwining foliage and scrollwork motifs.</image-desc>

I faithfully exhort and warn every Christian who wishes to practice this Art to abstain from all vanity, especially from anger and all other evil traits. Keep this one <term>Arcanum</term> <note>original: *Arcanum*; a profound secret or "mystery" of nature known only to initiates</note> hidden from all great lords for many reasons, as great evil would be caused thereby.

The Nesolon is intended for nothing more than to be applied to the <term>Albuchest</term> <note>original: *Albuchest*; likely a variation of Alkahest, a term used by alchemists to describe a universal solvent or a specific prepared mercurial base</note>, and to <term>tincture</term> <note>original: *thingieren*; to chemically transform or "color" a base metal into gold or silver</note> no other metal. This way is in itself simple and plain in its labor, whereas other great tinctures require much trouble and work in their preparation; among many thousands, hardly one can be found who encounters such a secret. For in this, the kind-hearted and faithful God in Heaven looks upon the person and the heart for which it is qualified—those who gladly call upon Him in prayer and persevere heartily, so that He might grant them success in this work; not for themselves alone, but for the benefit of the poor and needy, that through it, one might understand the treasure of great wisdom. I have possessed this treasure with honor, and in the <term>reiteration</term> <note>the process of repeating a sequence to increase the potency of the alchemical stone</note> of the <term>multiplication</term> <note>the final stage of the Great Work where the power of the medicine is increased exponentially</note>, I tinctured 1,000 parts with one part. I took little joy in it myself, only passing the time with the poor; when I distributed something to them, their thanksgiving to God the Most High was heard.

I also knew two men who possessed this Art, to whom God gave it even though they were wicked men. They practiced every evil desire with it, for their hearts were full of villainy, and they spoke all manner of evil against their neighbors. O, woe to your false mouths! You give a man very good, smooth words to his face, yet your heart is full of all wicked cunning. These men, on account of their pride and false trickery, and their fleshly desires, were torn into many thousand pieces by the devil.

# The Nefolon of Salomon Trismosin.

...from gold leaf <note>original: *Goltschlägern*; literally "gold-beaters," referring to the thin leaf they produce</note>, purely weighed, one fourth part. Take twice the weight of the upper Salt with a slight addition. Grind these pieces on a marble for six hours / then put the substance in a clean glass / and pour the upper **spirit of wine** <note>original: *spiritum vini*; distilled alcohol</note> over it / so that it rises two fingers high / place a still-head upon it in a **water bath** <note>original: *Bal. Mar.*, short for *Balneum Mariae*</note> and distill the spirit of wine fifteen <term>finger-breadths</term> <note>original: *Fingerschlag*; likely a measurement of the liquid level or a specific duration</note> away from it / and pour the spirit of wine back onto it / continue this drawing on and off / until the **gold** <note>original: *☉* (Sol)</note> becomes volatile / put it to the test / upon a glowing coal / see if it is volatile / if it smokes. Once it has become spiritualized / draw the essence off until dry / and <term>hermetically seal</term> <note>original: *persigillier*; from the "Seal of Hermes," making a container airtight</note> the glass / place in gentle heat / so that it coagulates well into a stone / yet does not rise up. And thus it is to be known / that the work can and must happen in one single glass / provided it is a good one. Take this stone with the glass / set it to <term>putrefy</term> <note>original: *putrificieren*; the process of breaking down a substance through gentle, moist heat</note> in horse manure / let it stand until the stone turns to water / and dissolves / take the glass / place it again in sifted ashes for three days / with very gentle heat / until it coagulates back into a stone / put this back into <term>horse manure</term> <note>original: *fimum equinum*</note> to dissolve / until it becomes water. Perform this coagulating and dissolving thirty times / or until it no longer allows itself to be coagulated / then there remains an incombustible **liquid** <note>original: *liquor*</note> / and it is a **tincture** in its essence perfectly prepared. Therefore you should faithfully thank God in your heart and praise Him highly.

**Note:** It is to be observed / that when it has been dissolved and coagulated fifteen times / the stone no longer begins to rise.

## To Tincture.

Take fifteen parts of purified **mercury** <note>original: *☿* (Mercury)</note> / put this into a small glass / pour one part of this prepared tincture upon it / seal the glass well at the top / place in sifted ashes for eight days / with gentle heat / thus it coagulates the mercury into pure tincture.

Take half a part of the coagulated mercury to 100 parts of raw purified mercury / when it begins to smoke / let them drive together for a while / then pour it out / that is the best **gold** <note>original: *☉* (Sol)</note>.

I state the conclusion / when you well <term>calcine</term> <note>original: *calcionierst*; to reduce a substance to powder through high heat</note> the stone of the whitest Nefolon / and burn it out with twice as much **tartar** <note>original: *Tartaro*</note> / and let this happen with fresh tartar for a third time / always dissolving it again / until an incombustible liquid remains. This liquid you may coagulate with a metallic **sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur*</note> / and use further for a tincture.

# The Tincture of the Philosopher Trismosin

...has been found that a <term>tincture</term> <note>a potent alchemical substance capable of transforming base metals into gold</note> manifested itself, intending to tincture silver into gold. In <term>stibnite</term> <note>original: *Spießglaß*; the naturally occurring mineral form of antimony sulfide</note>, which is called <term>antimony</term> <note>original: *Antimonium*</note>, there is a glimmering stone, gray and blackish in appearance, white on the inside, with a great redness within. In this, much of the <term>Sun</term> <note>original symbol: ☉; representing gold</note> is to be found. Whoever can separate it from the antimonial sulfur through art has enough to sustain himself. It is called the *hidden sun* <note>original: *sol obscurum*</note> because it is not visibly noticed in the antimony due to the large amount of sulfur which covers the gold. Whenever the antimony rises in the fire, it always carries this *hidden sun* with it, and it is also called the *elevated sun* <note>original: *sol eleuatum*</note> by many philosophers.

I say further: if the antimony were not mixed with gold, then "mountain gold" <note>natural, mined gold</note> would not become so pure and clear or so high in grade when poured through it. For the *elevated sun* <note>the "spirit" of gold within the antimony</note>, alongside the sulfur of antimony, tinctures common mountain gold so highly that it lacks nothing in any trial and stands perfect in all its power.

Therefore, a tincture can indeed be drawn from antimony because the *Sun* <note>gold</note> is within it; otherwise, if the gold were not there, there would be little to hope for from the antimony or its sulfur.

And know that gold, in the secret art, is the greatest essence in the world. It tinctures even common, poor, and imperfect sulfur so that they take on a golden nature, more than can be believed. I have experienced this with great effort and great expense.

But the fact that <term>any commoner</term> <note>original: *Heynz oder Cuntz*; a German idiom similar to "Tom, Dick, or Harry," referring to unskilled or uninitiated people</note> cannot find the right "grip" on gold to make it tincture as he would like is of little consequence. Even if you were to carry the gold over the <term>helm</term> <note>the top part of a still or alembic</note> twenty times or make it "spiritual" <note>volatile or gaseous</note>, the philosopher Trismosin says that nothing will be achieved by it.

The crude artists say that when they have brought the gold to a "spiritual" state, it is the <term>First Matter</term> <note>original: *prima materia*; the primordial starting material of the universe sought by alchemists</note>. Indeed, they are far mistaken! Make it into a "Philosophical Gold" first, then the *First Matter* will appear—if you understand it correctly, says Trismosin.

Now, a tincture is drawn from antimony, though it is not as perfect as that drawn from gold alone. It is commonly called an "Oily Tincture," directed toward <term>running mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿; quicksilver</note> and not toward all metals, as some imagine who wish to tincture many hundreds of pounds of other metals with it. Yet, this tincture transforms 1,000 parts of running mercury with one single part of itself into the best gold, durable in all tests. I have therefore [brought] forth a tincturing process with antimony...

### Thus prepare the stibnite for extraction.

Take two pounds of <term>antimony</term> <note>original: *Antimonium*</note> of the best quality you can obtain, which is easily found. From this, make a beautiful red <term>glass</term> <note>original: *rot Glaß*; "glass of antimony" was a translucent red substance created by the partial oxidation and fusion of the mineral</note> according to common practice. Afterward, let it <term>coagulate</term> <note>thicken or solidify</note> slowly in a gentle heat. Break the glass, grind the material fine, and put it back into a <term>flask</term> <note>original: *Urinalglaß*</note>. Pour the following sharp vinegar over it. Let it stand for eight days and nights. Afterward, pour the vinegar off into another glass; pour more fresh vinegar over the residue and let it extract for three days and nights. Repeat this with fresh vinegar until it no longer draws out any redness. Take all the poured-off vinegar into one glass and <term>distill</term> <note>original: *zeuch... ab*</note> it in an <term>ash bath</term> <note>original: *Eschen*; a container of hot ashes used to provide uniform heat</note> until dry; then you will have the <term>flowers of antimony</term> <note>original: *flores Antimonij*; the volatile sublimate or essence of the mineral</note> in the glass.

Put these flowers of antimony into a fresh glass onto which you can place a <term>distillation head</term> <note>original: *Helm*; an alembic or cap for capturing vapors</note>, and pour the prepared hellish, burning <term>spirit of sal ammoniac</term> <note>original: *Geist Salmiac*</note>—the preparation of which follows later—over it so that it covers it significantly. Set this to <term>putrefy</term> <note>to break down through gentle warmth</note> with gentle heat in a <term>water bath</term> <note>original: *Balneum Mariæ*; literally "Mary's Bath," a double-boiler setup</note> for three days and nights. Then distill it into a <term>receiving flask</term> <note>original: *Fürlegglaß*</note>. At first do this gently, then increasingly stronger. First, the burning spirit of sal ammoniac rises; afterward comes a blood-red oil of many colors. Continue the heat until no more red drops emerge. The <term>Oil of Antimony</term> <note>original: *Oleum Antimonij*</note> will remain in the glass, brownish-red or dark red in color.

Take this glass, seal it well at the top, and place it in the ash bath with very gentle heat. Let it slowly <term>coagulate</term> into a stone. Afterward, take the glass and place it with the matter back into moist horse dung or a water bath so that it <term>resolves</term> <note>turns back into liquid</note>. Then coagulate it again. Continue this process of dissolving and coagulating until it will no longer solidify and remains as an unburnable oil. This work is completed within thirty days and nights, and the oil is then prepared.

## The Vinegar Follows.

Take one pound of the very best white <term>calcined</term> <note>heated to a high temperature to reduce it to a powder</note> <term>tartar</term> <note>original: *Weinstain*; potassium bitartrate, the sediment found in wine barrels</note>. Distill it off once more. Do this "up and down" <note>pouring back and redistilling</note> four times, and so the vinegar will become very sharp.

## Now follows the hellish burning Spirit of Sal Ammoniac.

Take a pound of genuine <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>original: *Salmiar*; ammonium chloride</note> and one and a half pounds of common <term>molten salt</term>. Grind these two together finely. <term>Sublime</term> <note>the process of heating a substance so it turns to vapor and solidifies again at the top of the vessel</note> them in a <term>sublimation vessel</term>. Do this until the sal ammoniac becomes a tender, intangible <term>spirit</term> <note>a volatile substance or gas</note>. Collect this and grind it upon a smooth stone; afterward, put it into a glass and sprinkle it with strong <term>brandy</term> <note>original: *Brantenwein*</note> that has been prepared by filtering it seven times through <term>Venetian paper</term> <note>a high-quality, fine-pored paper used for chemical filtration</note>. Mar.* or *Balneum Mariae*; a water bath used for gentle heating</note> until the spirit has sublimated well. Pour off what has not <term>dissolved</term> <note>original: *soluiert*</note>. <term>Putrefy</term> <note>allow to break down through gentle warmth</note> that [undissolved] part again until everything is dissolved, then pour it off. Whatever refuses to dissolve should be sublimated again through molten salt and then dissolved again in the Mary's Bath.
When everything is dissolved into water, put the water into a tall <term>cucurbit</term> <note>original: *Kolbenglaß*; a long-necked flask used in distillation</note> and distill it in the Mary’s Bath until half is gone. Pour the distilled water back in and draw it off once more. Then increase the heat strongly until everything comes over the <term>alembic</term> <note>original: *Helm*; the "cap" of the still where vapors condense</note>. Then <term>rectify</term> <note>purify a liquid by repeated distillation</note> it until it gives off or leaves behind no more <term>sediment</term> <note>original: *feces*</note>. # T I N C T U R E
->The Geroton of Salomon Trismosin.<-
<note>original: *Geroton*; likely a title or a corrupted reference to a "secret" or "sacred" work attributed to Trismosin, the legendary teacher of Paracelsus.</note>

**This tincture is to be brought through its solution in such a way that it eventually transmutes 1,000 parts of imperfect metal into the best gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note>. The dissolution is achieved with simple things, turning them into a spiritual essence; however, a skilled worker is required who understands the sequence of colors.**

I want to tell you, who wish to work this tincture, that you must be God-fearing and righteous in your prayer, and especially ask Almighty God that He would grant His Holy Spirit to this work and graciously kindle the right fire for this tincture. But if you are a fornicator and will not desist from your evil intentions, and do not renounce and swear off spending your life in lechery, then I advise you not to begin the tinctural work. Even if you were able to complete it, you would still be punished with death while in your sin. For it is such a great mystery that barely one in a thousand finds it by the will of God, and among them, there is only one to whom it is truly given. This mystery and revelation occurs only for the benefit of the poor, just as this mystery was given by the Highest to pagan and also some Christian kings who were pious, as a comfort to the poor. The righteous Lord of Heaven and Earth knows your fornicating and knavish heart and your rogue's mind—what you intend to do with it. And I faithfully advise you: if you do not seek this work from God first, then let it rest; otherwise, you would surely lose body and soul. He willingly lets Himself be entreated, but on the other hand, He punishes harshly if it is not used rightly; watch yourself, I, Trismosin, tell you.

Furthermore, in the first <term>coagulation</term> <note>the process of solidifying a liquid or gas, often the first sign of successful refinement</note> you must be knowledgeable about the colors, and especially about the first color, called the <term>crow’s head</term> <note>original: *caput corvi*; a technical term for the 'nigredo' or blackening stage, symbolizing the death of the base material before its transformation</note>, which manifests so erratically many times that it makes even an experienced philosopher foolish. Indeed, it is said that it becomes black; yes, dear reader, tell me, once you have worked out a tincture, whether the first color remains black, gray, or the color of earth, yet appears reddish to the eye.

# Karaseton of Trismosin.

## Arcanum for Running Mercury.

Whoever wishes to use this solution <note>original: *Solution*</note> should not produce an excess of silver from the running mercury <note>original symbol: ☿; liquid quicksilver</note>, or the art will turn to water for him. # Paraseton of Trismosin.

Hold your tongue, and do not strut about in fine clothes, for God cannot abide pride.

## This solution is called Paraseton, used for a volatile metal that is to be employed in Balbale <note>possibly a corruption of *Balneum Mariae* (water bath) or a specific alchemical vessel</note>.

Take one and a half pounds of Sal Ammoniac <note>ammonium chloride</note>; crush it small and place it into a glazed vessel. Over this, pour an old, strong, high-quality wine so that it covers it well. The wine should be warm; thus the spirit will be drawn into the wine, and the soot <note>the residue or impurities</note> will sit at the bottom <note>original: *in fundo*</note> for twelve hours. Pour the wine off gently into another glazed vessel. Simmer this very lightly—not entirely, but until reduced by half—and place it in a cold spot overnight. Afterward, pour off the wine, and you will find crystals; use them as follows.

### How to prepare the Spirit of Wine for the work.

Take one and a half measures of strong Easter brandy <note>original: *Osterbrandwein*, a high-proof distilled spirit</note> in a glass. Place a four-fold Venetian paper <note>a high-quality paper used for filtration or as a gasket</note> over it. Distill the spirit of wine <note>original: *Spiritum*</note> from it according to common practice, so that the water remains behind in more than half the volume; then it is prepared.

### How to operate.

Take two lots <note>a *Loth* is a traditional German weight, roughly 1/2 ounce or 15 grams</note> of leaf-stone <note>original: *Felch folion*, likely a mineral leaf or a specific metallic foil</note> and three lots of the aforementioned crystals. Grind these two pieces very fine upon a marble stone together for two hours. Afterward, place these into a flask <note>original: *Kolbenglaß*</note> or a flat crucible, and pour the aforementioned spirit of wine over them so that it covers them well. Draw it off <note>distill it</note> very gently and pour it back on again; and again draw it off. This must be done with fresh spirit until the volatility appears everywhere upon a glowing flask. 

Afterward, draw off the spirit until it is dry; this must all be done in a Mary’s bath <note>original: *Bal. Mar.*, a double boiler used for gentle heating</note>. Now take the glass with the substance—which is not yet entirely dry, but rather a thick liquor—and set it in clean, swept ashes <note>an ash bath, used for even, dry heat</note>. Let it coagulate <note>solidify</note> very gently into a white salt. Watch this with great care so that it does not rise <note>sublime or vaporize</note>, but keep it at a constant warmth for eighteen days and nights until you perceive that it no longer desires to rise. 

Afterward, strengthen the fire even more; at this degree, it will turn to a gray color. Then strengthen the fire even more and keep it steady; it will become a beautiful white, and thereafter "over-white" <note>extremely brilliant white</note>, like a glittering Canary sugar. It is then prepared to coagulate Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note>.

Let the mercury smoke away in a sand bath. Afterward, take the powder into a Venetian glass, pour a *jaforon* <term>Jaforon: likely a "Saffron" or orange-colored chemical oil, possibly an iron or gold precipitate</term> over it, and precipitate it into a stone; thus the powder is fixed. Take this with a fast-flowing flux, half as heavy, and let it melt strongly in a crucible. Then a regulus will settle. Refine this by cupellation with lead <term>original: ♄num</term>. This is "Fixed Silver" <term>Luna fix: silver that has been chemically "fixed" so that it resists traditional tests of acid or heat, often intended to mimic the properties of gold</term>, stable, and excellent in weight in all tests.

## The Cement thereafter.

Take common salt, raw vitriol <term>Vittruat: an archaic spelling of vitriol, likely copper or iron sulfate</term>, and steel filings—half a pound of each. Grind them together finely, place them in a crucible, and let them macerate in a charcoal fire <term>Kolfewr: a fire fueled by coals, capable of steady heat</term> for three hours. Grind it fine again and extract it with good wine vinegar until nothing more is drawn out. Evaporate all of this vinegar or draw it off until it reaches an oily consistency. Take three parts brick dust <term>Zigelmel: powdered brick, used as a carrier in cementation</term>, one part Hungarian vitriol, and two parts sal ammoniac. Pour the oiliness over this and let it dry into a powder. With this, cement the "Fixed Moon" <term>Luna fix: silver that has been treated to withstand heat or chemical change</term>.

# A very proven work with a coagulated Mercury that stands in the fire for many hours.

Take Jumelon <term>Jumelon: an alchemical term likely referring to a "twin" substance or a specific antimony compound</term> and vitriol, one pound of each; boil them in urine four times. Afterward, place this material in a crucible, let it flow strongly, and cast a loth <note>approximately 15-16 grams</note> of common sulfur into it about once. Then pour out the regulus <term>König: literally "king"; the metallic button that settles at the bottom of the crucible</term>. Let this smoke away until it reaches the pits <note>original: *Gruben*; likely referring to a specific state of the residue or the depressions in the vessel</note>, then crush it very fine. Grind into it half its weight of running mercury <term>☿: the symbol for Mercury</term> that has previously been made into a paste with common sulfur. Cement the mercury in a closed vessel gently in a charcoal fire. Take this Jumelon and twice as much coagulated mercury (which has been coagulated without metal and holds for many hours in the fire). Grains this fine and mix it into the Jumelon. Put it all together into a good glass vessel. Over this, pour a Jasoron <term>Jasoron: a rare alchemical term for a specific dissolving water or solvent</term> in which four parts of fine silver have been dissolved. Precipitate it into a stone and grind it small. Take an equal weight of the following "Flux" and put it together in a crucible. Let it start gently in a wind furnace <term>Windoffen: a furnace that uses a natural or forced draft to reach high temperatures</term> and then more strongly, so that a regulus will settle. Place this on a cupel <term>Treibscherben: a shallow, porous dish for refining</term> with twice as much lead. Let it work until the "silver flowers" <term>Silberblumen: a visual phenomenon during cupellation indicating purity</term> appear, and refine it on the cupel until the "flash" <note>the *Blick*, the moment a precious metal becomes pure and reflective</note>. This is a very excellent Gold <term>☉: the symbol for Gold</term> in all tests. It is proven.

## Flux.

Take raw tartar <term>Weinstein: potassium bitartrate</term> and saltpeter <term>Saliter: potassium nitrate</term>, four loth of each. Calcify or burn it off. Take the burnt tartar and an equal amount of fresh saltpeter and burn it off once more. This should be done a third time. Then take half as much fresh saltpeter as the burnt tartar weighs, and also the same amount of arsenic and half a loth of iron filings. Grind everything small together, and the Flux is then ready.

## An even faster process with fixed sulfur.

Take purified fine silver—as described in the first section—of the smoked-off tin with antimony, and cement the same with mercury <term>☿: the alchemical symbol for quicksilver or mercury</term> and sulfur; also a coagulated mercury without metal that can withstand the fire for many hours. Take eight loth <note>A loth is a traditional German unit of weight, approximately 15–16 grams</note> of each; let them melt strongly together, and add four loth of fixed sulfur <term>Fixed sulfur: sulfur that has been chemically treated so it no longer evaporates when heated</term> onto it. Let it flow in the heat for four hours; thereafter, refine it until the "brightening" <term>blick: the "silver flash," a sudden brightening of the metal's surface that signals the end of the purification process</term>. This is an excellent gold.

It would be very good if a fixed sulfur was made *by itself* <note>original: *per se*</note> with its own oiliness <note>original: *feistigkeit*; refers to the alchemical concept of a substance's "fatness" or essential combustible principle</note>, and that not many foreign substances were added to it; this would be very useful for such matters. Some wish to make fixed sulfur by using coarse, infusible substances; these lead them to a point where the material can no longer be melted, especially those where a lye is made with lime and ashes.

## With the following sulfur, five loth of gold <term>☉: the symbol for gold or the Sun</term> can be brought into a mark of silver.

Take white arsenic <note>original: *Arsenicum Album*</note>, common sulfur, and antimony—four loth of each. Let them melt together in a glass vessel (beware of the smoke). Let this cool, and take half of it; put this in a glass and pour a strong Jasoron <term>Iasoron: a specialized alchemical solvent or "water" mentioned previously in the text</term> over it. Precipitate it and keep it for when it is needed.

Take the other half and an equal weight of Jumelon <term>Iumelon: an alchemical substance, likely a specific salt or mineral compound, used as a flux or reagent</term> that is of good quality, and calcine it with the sulfur in a clean pot between two bricks in a charcoal glow, until the tin lies there like "pits" <note>original: *Grüben*; likely referring to a porous or pitted residue left in the vessel</note>. Mix this with half as much cinnabar <term>Zinober: mercury sulfide, a bright red mineral</term> and let the cinnabar smoke away from it. Take this tin and an equal weight of the precipitate mentioned above; into this, knead <note>original: *impastier*</note> raw mercury of equal weight. Let them melt strongly together and add four loth of lead <term>♄: the symbol for lead or Saturn</term> into it, so that a regulus <term>König: literally "king"; the heavy metallic button that settles at the bottom of a crucible after smelting</term> will settle. Refine this with an equal weight of fine silver on a cupel <note>A shallow, porous bowl used in assaying to separate precious metals from lead</note> and thereafter until the "brightening." The silver will then contain five loth of gold for every mark <note>A mark is a unit of weight for precious metals, roughly 233 grams</note>. It is proven <note>original: *Probatum*</note>.

## The Secret Cement Jumelothon.

Take cinnabar, arsenic, raw sulfur <note>original: *Chybur*; an archaic term for sulfur</note>, and antimony—two loth <note>A loth is a traditional German unit of weight, approximately 15–16 grams</note> of each; grind them all together.

Take 23 loth of white calcined tartar <term>Weinstein: tartar or potassium bitartrate, often used as a flux in melting</term>, good English tin, and vitriol <term>Vitriat: a sulfate mineral, often iron or copper sulfate</term>—one pound of each—and four loth of verdigris <term>Grünspan: the green pigment or crust that forms on copper</term>. Let these melt together strongly, and pour out the regulus <term>König (literally "king"): the purified metallic portion that settles at the bottom of a crucible</term>. Keep this; let the slag <note>original: *Schlacken*</note> melt again, then pour out another regulus and add it to the previous one. Let it melt, and repeat this with the slag until no more regulus settles.

Let all the reguli evaporate <note>original: *abrauchen*; to heat until volatile components are driven off</note> thoroughly until a residue remains; grind this small and keep it for when it is needed. Take the slag, ground fine, and lay it upon a dissolving stone <note>original: *Soluierstein*; a slab used to let substances absorb moisture from the air and liquefy</note>, and moisten it with brandy <note>original: *Brantenwein*; literally "burnt wine," or distilled spirits</note>. In a cold place, a water will trickle down from it over several days. Now take the four sulfurs mentioned above, ground fine together, and mix in the residue from the regulus. Put everything into a glass and pour all the trickled-down water over it. Let it slowly coagulate to dryness in a sand bath; then it will begin to melt. Let it sit for a while, let it cool, then grind it small. Keep it in an earthenware vessel, but ensure it always remains in a warm place.

However, I wish to have everyone warned here that they should take great care regarding these poisonous things, especially when they smoke in the fire. When one grinds them, such a smoke enters into you that you can hardly remove the poison from your body. Arsenic settles immediately upon the liver and strikes the heart; within 16 hours you will no longer have life. Therefore, where there are good miners, when they wish to go to work, they eat fresh butter and drink bitter wormwood wine; be warned.

Take two loth of the cement powder and one loth of finely granulated silver <note>original: *Felch*; an archaic term for silver, often associated with fine or granulated metal</note>; put them together in a crucible <note>original: *Digel*</note>. Let it sit for nine hours: three hours gently with a mild charcoal fire <note>original: *Kolfewr*</note>, and then increasingly strong and even stronger. Thereafter, carry the
->material into the lead; refine it until the "brightening," which results in<-
->an excellent gold <term>☉: the alchemical symbol for gold or the Sun</term> in all<-
->tests.<-

# Trismosinian Treatise
### Concerning All Kinds of
# Sulfurous Pyrites,
### Also Concerning
# Fire-stone or Gun-flint,

### how they are to be used in the Chemical Art, and what benefit they provide, so that in many of them much gold <note>original: ☉</note> is preserved, so that a poor journeyman may well support and sustain himself with them; containing several "Particulars" <note>A "particular" refers to an alchemical process that transmutates a specific amount of metal, rather than the "universal" transformation of the Philosopher's Stone</note>.

---

## This is a small piece for a trial, as follows.

Take sulfurous gun-pyrite, roast it until red, and take raw antimony, raw tartar <term>Tartarum: potassium bitartrate, a byproduct of winemaking used as a flux</term>, three and a half loth <note>A *loth* is approximately 15–16 grams</note> of each; and one loth of steel filings. Grind everything together finely. Of this, take four loth and one loth of silver <note>original: ☽</note>; put them together in a crucible with the silver on top. Cover the crucible and place it in a wind-furnace. Let it flow strongly for an hour and a half, and a regulus <term>König: literally "king," the purified metal button that settles at the bottom of a crucible</term> will settle. Refine this by cupellation <note>original: *treib durch den ♄ ab*; a process of heating ore with lead to separate precious metals</note>. Afterward, do the same with the silver as before, letting the regulus pass through lead again, and you will have "fixed" silver <note>Silver that has been made resistant to chemical change, a step toward transmutation</note>.

## 1. Concerning a Marcasite that withstands glowing and gives a gold test.

Take such marcasite <note>A common iron sulfide mineral often mistaken for gold or silver ore</note> and roast one pound of it. Put it into a glass and pour a very strong aqua fortis <term>Aquafort: nitric acid, literally "strong water"</term> over it so that it is well covered. Let it stand for a day and night in gentle warmth. Then take common mercury <note>original: ☿</note> in a glass, and pour the extracted marcasite liquid over it. Precipitate this. Take four loth of fine silver <note>original: ☽</note> onto which mercury has previously been cast while in flux. Laminate this into thin sheets and perform *stratum super stratum* <note>Latin: "layer upon layer"</note> with the silver. Cement it for 7 hours, and it will become half gold <note>original: ☉</note>.

## 2. With gold slick.

Take gold slick <note>original: *Goldt ſchlicht*; the fine, silty residue or "slimes" from gold mining</note> that has not been roasted, according to your judgment. Calcinate <term>Calcionier: to reduce to a powder through heat</term> copper <note>original: ♀</note> foil with it. Take this and an equal weight of fine silver <note>original: ☽</note> containing no gold. For every two loth, take one loth of saltpeter and one loth of raw tartar; these should previously be moistened with urine. Let all of this melt for one hour, then refine it by cupellation with lead. This yields three loth of high-quality gold <note>original: ☉</note> for every mark <note>A *Marck* is a unit of weight, roughly 233 grams</note>.
