# CHAPTER THREE
## On the Composition of Matter and Form.

Now that you have prepared and finished the **Matter and Form** of the Stone (as has been shown), take 1 part of this last oil that you obtained from the **sublimated powder**. Put it into a new, clean little flask or glass bulb. Add to it many times as much <term>Water of Life</term> <note>original: *Aquæ vitæ*; here referring to highly distilled and purified alcohol</note>, which has been highly **rectified** <note>purified through repeated distillation</note> as described above. Seal the little flask well at the bottom with <term>Clay of Wisdom</term> <note>original: *Luto Sapientiæ*; a specialized airtight sealant used by alchemists, often made of clay, lime, and organic binders</note>, as is the custom. Place it in reasonably warm **ashes** <note>a "sand bath" or ash bath for indirect, even heating</note> and let it become quite warm, ensuring the glass is well-protected against the escape of vapors. Mix it well in this manner and immediately place its **blind helm** <note>original: *blindes Helmlein*; a distillation head without a spout, used to force vapors to condense and fall back into the mixture (reflux)</note> upon it. This helm should be coated with a mixture of **egg white and quicklime**, with a small ring of good <term>Clay of Wisdom</term> carefully applied over the joints and further secured with egg white.

Place this in a <term>Furnace</term> <note>original: *Fornacem*</note> that maintains a steady heat and is easy to control. Regulate it with a low heat. In this way, the oil and the <term>Water of Life</term> will dissolve into one another so that in 12 days—if one proceeds correctly—the **black color** appears. With the same fire or heat, during the next 8 days, the blackness turns to **white**, and after another eight days, it turns into **yellow**. If the heat is strengthened slightly, the yellow color also turns into **red** within eight days, looking like an egg.

Afterward, one must remove the little glass with the **Stone**, and clean the Stone of the filth and impurities that cling to the glass around it. Place the cleaned Stone into another clean little glass, just like the previous one. Regulate it in the furnace again for 6 days and nights, but with a slightly stronger fire—specifically, so hot that one cannot easily bear to keep a hand in the ashes where the glass stands. When you remove it after 6 days, the <term>Animal Stone</term> <note>original: *Lapis Animalis*; a stage of the alchemical work associated with a more "animated" or potent state of the matter</note> is completely finished.

->The Vegetable Stone follows.<-

To make the aforementioned **Animal Stone** into the <term>Vegetable Stone</term> <note>original: *Lapidem Vegetabilem*; in alchemy, the "Vegetable" stage often refers to the Stone's ability to "grow" or multiply its power</note>: Take again, for example, if you had four <term>Loth</term> <note>a historical unit of weight, roughly 1/2 ounce or 15 grams</note> of the oil from the sublimated powder, and add three times that weight—which is 12 <term>Loth</term>—of <term>Water of Life</term>, and 1 <term>Quintlein</term> <note>a small unit of weight, about 4 grams</note> of the newly made <term>Animal Stone</term>. Put them together, mixed as before, and let them stand for 30 days, passing through the **colors** <note>original: *Colores*; the sequence of color changes (black, white, yellow, red) indicating the progress of the Great Work</note>. Thus you will have the <term>Vegetable Stone</term>.

## Following: Multiplication of the Stone.

If you then wish to multiply the <term>Stone</term> <note>original: *Lapidem*; the Philosopher's Stone</note> in <term>Virtue</term> <note>original: *Virtute*; referring to its inherent power or "potency" rather than moral virtue</note>, take as much of the aforementioned Stone as you wish and a third part as much <term>Water of Life</term> <note>original: *Aquæ Vitæ*; highly distilled alcohol or a specialized solvent</note>, and mix them as before. Set it in the heat and let it pass through the <term>Colors</term> <note>original: *Colores*; the characteristic color changes (black, white, yellow, red) that signal progress in the alchemical process</note>. Or, take the finished Stone and place it with a little Water of Life in a <term>Water Bath</term> <note>original: *Balneum*; a gentle heating method</note> to purify and congeal it, as mentioned above; this is better than setting it in as a powder. You may do this as often as you wish, and the Stone will become better the longer it is worked. For the more it is multiplied, the more it <term>tinges</term> <note>original: *tingirt*; the alchemical ability of the Stone to "dye" or transform the nature of a base metal into gold</note>. Namely: if it originally transmutes 10 parts and is multiplied once, it will then transmute 100 parts. The second time, 1,000 parts, and so on.

For the **White Work** <note>original: *Auff das Weiß*; the process of creating the Silver Stone</note>, one uses exactly the same labor, except that in the beginning, one requires no <term>Antimony</term> <note>original: *Antimonium*</note> or <term>Cement</term> <note>a corrosive powder used in refining</note> to finish the silver. Instead, one refines the silver two or three times on the <term>Cupel</term> <note>original: *Capellen*; a shallow porous vessel used in assaying and refining precious metals</note> to the highest degree, makes it fine, and beats it into a round plate. The colors come again: the first color is **Green**, the second **Red**, the third **White**, and the fourth is the metal, white as silver. Otherwise, the process is the same for one as it is for the other.

## Following: The Projection.

Now you should know that when you wish to <term>cast upon</term> <note>original: *auffwerffen*; the act of "Projection," adding the Stone to molten base metal</note>, you will find no metal that accepts the substance of the <term>Blessed Stone</term> <note>original: *Lapidis Benedicti*</note> into itself more readily than gold (where the Stone has been prepared for the **Red Work**). For the **White Work**, however, silver is most pleasant to it. Therefore, upon whichever of these two you wish to cast, throw 1 part of your **Medicine** upon 100 parts of gold flowing in the crucible. Then, throw one part of that same gold again upon 100 parts of gold flowing in the crucible, and so on as long as it pleases you. When you have sufficiently multiplied it in the gold—for this is the **Multiplication in Quantity**—then throw 1 part of this same gold (which is now also Medicine) upon 100 parts of <term>Imperfect Body</term> <note>original: *Corporis Imperfecti*; a base metal like lead or tin</note> or <term>Raw Quicksilver</term> <note>original: *Argenti Viui Crudi*; mercury</note>, and refine it on the test. Then you will truly have gold, equal to all proofs and eternally lasting.

If your Stone is multiplied to the <term>Highest Perfection</term> <note>original: *ad summam Perfectionem*</note> in virtue, or also in quantity, multiplied in gold alone, then you may dissolve it again in a <term>Water Bath</term> <note>original: *Balneo*</note>. It is then **Drinkable Gold** <note>original: *Aurum Potabile*; a legendary alchemical medicine believed to have restorative and life-extending properties</note>. Not only all imperfect...

-># In the Universal and Particular Way.<-

Metals are good to transform into true Gold and Silver through **Projection** <note>The act of casting a small amount of the Stone onto a large mass of molten base metal to effect transformation</note> alone, as mentioned; moreover, it is the highest **Medicine** <note>original: *Medicin*; in alchemy, the "Medicine" refers to the Stone’s ability to "heal" base metals into gold or human bodies into health</note> for metallic bodies that exists on Earth.

You may also immediately cast 1 part of the <term>Medicine</term> <note>original: *Medicinæ*</note> onto 1,000 parts of <term>Raw Quicksilver</term> <note>original: *Argenti Viui Crudi*; common mercury</note>, or common mercury, when it is warm in the **crucible** <note>original: *Tigel*; a ceramic or graphite container used for melting metals at high temperatures</note>; thus it becomes a red powder. For this Medicine has the greatest attachment and affinity for metals.

If it is dissolved entirely into water, or much better into oil, then it has its greatest effect in human **bodies** <note>original: *Corporibus*</note>, or other living animals; for this reason, **inceration** <note>original: *Inceratio*</note> was also invented.

### The First Part.

When you have now prepared the **Lunaria** <term>original: *Lunariam*; likely a silver-based solvent or "moon-water"</term> and the **Water of Life** <term>original: *Aquam Vitæ*; usually distilled alcohol or a potent solvent</term> (as mentioned above in the Second Part), it is not yet entirely finished as it should be. Then take the pregnant Earth, lay it in a **Sublimatorium** <term>a vessel used for sublimation—turning a solid into vapor and back to solid</term> made of clay, well-sealed for 24 hours; **sublimate** it, so that the pure may be separated from the impure. **Imbibe** <note>to moisten or soak a dry substance with a liquid</note> this sublimated **Salt of Tartar** with an equal part of **Lunaria**, set it to putrefy for 3 days in a **Balneum** <note>original: *Balneum*; a water bath or Bain-marie</note>, then draw the water down again with a gentle fire in the ashes. And calcine the Earth, imbibe it, and putrefy it again; distill and calcine it as before, and do this four times. Then set it by itself in a water bath to dissolve, and congeal it again; do this also four times, then you have the true **Salt of Tartar**, or **Vegetable Salt**. This Salt, which is thus dissolved and coagulated by itself, is called in great secrecy by the **Philosophers** <note>the alchemists of old</note> the **Philosophical Ointment** <term>original: *Vnguentum Philosophicum*</term>.

For the metallic bodies, one must take 1 pound of **quicksilver**, put the same into a glass, and pour onto it the previously mentioned **fortified** <note>original: *acuirter*; sharpened or made more chemically active</note> Lunaria, so that it covers it by four fingers-breadth. Let it stand for 6 days in a warm water bath, and it will dissolve. Of this water, which is now mixed with the **Quicksilver** <note>original: *Argento Viuo*</note>, take 1 pound, mixed with 7 pounds of the previous Lunaria. With this, one dissolves all metallic bodies, for otherwise it is impossible for the metals to rise upward in **sublimation** <note>the process where a solid turns into vapor and then back into solid without becoming a liquid</note>. Therefore, take of this Lunaria, which was previously circulated for 60 days and afterwards mixed with common quicksilver (as mentioned), and dissolve the metals which were previously **calcined** <note>reduced to powder through intense heat</note> by <term>Mercury</term> <gloss>Mercury</gloss> <note>original: the symbol ☿</note> in all the ways indicated above, throughout until it has been set as one should sublimate. For when that same sublimation has occurred, then the first part, and [a work of] Philosophy in this regard concerning the **Transmutation of Metals**, is completed.

The **dregs** <note>original: *Fæces*; the solid residue or sediment left over after a chemical process</note> that remain behind are the **calcined gold** <note>gold reduced to a fine powder through intense heat</note> or the **sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur*; in alchemy, this refers to the active, combustible principle of a substance</note>; keep that. But the water drawn from it is the **Lunaria** <note>original: *Lunaria*; literally "moon-water," a solvent believed to be related to the powers of silver or the moon</note>, sharpened with the gold, which you should **rectify** <note>the process of purifying a liquid by repeated distillation</note> twice.

With this sharpened Lunaria, dissolve the **Sulfur of Nature** <note>original: *Sulphur Naturę*; the inherent vital energy or essence within a substance</note> which you produced in the **sublimation** <note>the process where a solid turns directly into a gas and then back to a solid, used to purify substances</note>, into a pure poured-off water, just as you initially did with the calcined gold. Take this entire moisture and set it immediately, without any further putrefaction, into the **water bath** <note>original: *Balneum*; a method of heating using a container of water to ensure gentle, even warmth</note>. Draw the water down with the very gentlest heat, so that the **Air** <note>original: *Aër*; the alchemical element of volatility and movement</note> remains at the bottom. But over the dregs, which previously remained in the glass in the ashes during the distillation, put the water again—the water you just drew from the Air—and putrefy it for two days. Distill it again in the ashes and take the water in the water bath. Begin this process again, repeating it twelve times. And when you have brought all the Air together, rectify it seven times in **ashes** <note>original: *Cinere*; using warm ash as a heat source for distillation</note>. The dregs that it leaves behind in each rectification should be added to the dregs that remained from the twelve distillations in the ashes mentioned above. These same dregs, in which the **Fire** <note>the alchemical element of heat and transformation</note> is contained, should be rubbed small on a glass plate. Pour the whole water that you drew from the Air onto it. Set it to putrefy for three days, distill it in sand, and dry it out well so that all moisture comes out. Set this same moisture in the water bath and draw the water from it with the gentlest warmth; what then remains at the bottom of the glass is the Fire.

Place the water over the dregs again, putrefy it again as before, and treat it in all things as you did previously. Do this eight times. And whatever you have extracted from the Fire, rectify that also seven times. Likewise, the dregs that the Fire always leaves behind should be added to the **Earth** <note>original: *Erdtrich*; the solid, fixed residue</note> or dregs that remained behind. But the water drawn from all these separations must also be rectified seven times in the water bath. Keep these three **liquors** <note>original: *Liquores*; alchemical liquids or essences</note>, each individually in well-secured glasses, and mark them so that you do not take or grasp one for the other when you wish to use them.

...is just as heavy, and a third part as heavy as the **calcined gold** <note>gold reduced to a fine powder through intense heat</note>, or **sulfur**, and likewise of the oil—that is, the **Philosophical Ointment** <term>Vnguenti Philosophici</term>—is also as heavy as the **earth** <note>the solid residue remaining at the bottom of the flask</note> is. After twelve days, add as much water again by weight; let it putrefy again, and continue doing this until the twelve parts of water have been added. 

Afterwards, take the **Air** <note>original: *Aërem*; likely referring to a volatile distilled fraction</note>, divide it into eight parts; put one part into the glass with the previous mixture and let it putrefy for eight days. Thereafter, add another part, and so on, until all eight are in. ### Multiplication.

Afterwards, take this stone and dissolve it with three times its weight of **Lunaria** <note>the alchemical solvent "moon-water" previously prepared</note> which has been sharpened with gold. Also add a third part, by weight of the **stone** <term>Lapis</term>, of calcined gold—which is called sulfur—and let it putrefy in a **water bath** <note>original: *Balneo*</note> for twelve days. Put it again into the fixing-glass, as before, and let it pass through the **colors** <note>the sequence of color changes—black, white, yellow, red—indicating the progress of the alchemical Work</note> with a gentle fire for twelve days, or until it is finished. And in this way, you may multiply it **in power** <note>original: *in Virtute*</note> as often as you wish.

You may also multiply it **in power and quantity** <note>original: *in Virtute, & Quantitate*</note> together, namely: if you put four parts of calcined gold or sulfur, and one part of the prepared **stone** <term>Lapide</term>, as well as twelve parts of the sharpened Lunaria together into putrefaction, it will dissolve in four days. Then, as before, take the fourth or sixth part of the moisture through distillation with the "helm," and afterwards fix it as before. And the more often such **multiplication** is repeated, the more useful the stone is in **projection** <note>the final act of alchemy: throwing the finished stone onto base metal to transform it into gold</note>.

This multiplication may also be done in another way, namely: take **amalgamated gold**, made from one part gold and five parts **raw mercury** <term>☿ Crudi</term>; add four parts of the **amalgam** <term>Amalgamæ</term> to one **lot** <note>a historical unit of weight, roughly 15-16 grams</note> of the stone. Dissolve each separately, mixed with Lunaria, place it into the **Vessel of Hermes** <term>Vaß Hermetis</term>, and multiply it as often as you wish. With this, you produce just as much gold in proportion as otherwise.

# The Fourth Part.
## Preparation of the Mineral Stone.

To assemble the **Mineral Stone** in a short time, proceed as follows: Make an **Aqua fort** <term>Aqua fortis</term> <note>literally "strong water," usually nitric acid</note> from two pounds of **calcined vitriol** <note>iron or copper sulfate heated until it becomes a dry powder</note>, one pound of **saltpeter**, and one and a half pounds of **cinnabar** <note>mercury sulfide</note>. When it has been distilled as is customary, always add one and a half pounds of fresh cinnabar to each pound of the resulting water, and distill it again. Do this five times, so that you bring three pounds of cinnabar into one pound of water. Once this is done, take for every one pound of *Aqua fort*—thus sharpened with the cinnabar—one pound of **Lunaria** <note>original: *Lunariæ*; likely a reference to a specific alchemical liquor or "moon-water"</note>, which has been best sharpened with **Salt of Tartar** <term>Sale Tartari</term> <note>potassium carbonate</note>. Mix these together very gently, let it stand for one or two days in a warm **water bath** <term>Balneo</term>, so that it may be well incorporated, and afterwards distill it all together.

<margin>This salt is nobler than the Salt of Tartar.</margin>
If you now wish to make the **Vegetable Salt** <term>Sal Vegetabile</term>, then let it circulate for 16 days in the water bath; it will then unite at the bottom of the glass like a crystal glass. Keep this and use it in the Mineral Stone instead of the **Philosophical Ointment** <term>Unguenti Philosophici</term>. When you put your **calcined gold** into it, add one ounce of gold for every twelve ounces of the salt; set it to **putrefy** <note>to break down through gentle heat</note> for 20 days. Add also one ounce of the Philosophical Ointment, and everything will become pure water. Afterwards, place a **distillation lid** <note>original: *Helm*</note> upon it, and draw the water off in the water bath so that only the gold and what the water leaves behind remain at the bottom. **Congeal** <note>solidify</note> this in the ash-heat. When it has cooled well and you have opened the glass, weigh the material, and add exactly the same weight of the aforementioned mixed water and a very little of the Philosophical Ointment; dissolve it again in the water bath and **regulate** <note>original: *guliers*; likely *reguliers*, meaning to process or fix</note> it in the ash-heat. Do this ten times. Then take your dissolved powder; for every one ounce of powder, add twelve ounces of the best rectified *Lunaria*, sharpened with Salt of Tartar and Gold, and one ounce of calcined gold or sulfur. Circulate it all through the stage of putrefaction; put it into a **Hermetic Vessel** <term>Vas Hermetis</term> <note>a glass flask sealed with heat</note>, let it pass through all the **colors** <note>the traditional sequence of black, white, and red in the alchemical process</note> for 22 days, and **fix** it <note>render it stable under heat</note> if it is not finished before that time. However, I expect you will accomplish it in 10 or, at the longest, 12 days.

When this has been done, take this **medicine**; namely, when there are 12 ounces, add half an ounce of Philosophical Ointment. Putrefy them together for nine days in the water bath, then congeal it in the ash-heat. Dissolve it again by itself without any addition, and congeal it. Continue this until it no longer wishes to be congealed; then you have enough, and you can finish this medicine in 80 days.

# Multiplication of the Medicine. <note>original: *Multiplicatio Medicinæ*; the process of increasing the quantity and potency of the alchemical substance</note>

Multiply this medicine in this way: Take one ounce of this Stone in a glass and place upon it half an ounce of the **amalgam** <note>a blend of metals, usually involving mercury</note> made from one part gold and five parts **mercury**. Seal the glass with a **blind helm** <note>a distillation cap without a pouring spout, used to force vapors to condense and fall back into the vessel</note> and place it in warm ashes for six hours. When the material appears like gold, then stop; if not, continue with the fire until you see the sign, or until it turns into a red powder. Then take again a little of the **Philosophical Ointment** <term>Vnguento Philosophico</term> <note>a specialized alchemical substance used as a solvent or binder, previously described in the text</note>, use it to dissolve this powder, and congeal it again in the ashes. Repeat this until it will no longer allow itself to be congealed.

Then take one part of this final medicine; add it again to ten parts of amalgam in a sealed glass; dissolve it and congeal it. From that same medicine, take one part again, add it to ten parts of amalgam or common mercury, and proceed as before. Continue with this repetition for as long and as many times as needed until it no longer becomes a red powder but rather a hard, brittle **mass** <term>Massa</term>. Then cast some of it out and observe how much it **tinges** <note>original: *tingiere*; the act of the medicine "dyeing" or transforming a base metal into a noble one</note>. In this way, you will find the correct proportion—how many parts of mercury or imperfect metals you may transform with one part of this medicine—so that it becomes eternal, stable gold, as good as that which comes from the mines.

But if you wish to perform a **multiplication** that proceeds forever without end, then take some of the last medicine or "congelation" where the mass has become hard. Grind it, then take 50 parts by weight of common mercury (relative to the weight of the mass) and put them together in a well-secured glass. Let it stand in a constant, small, gentle heat for 30 days. It will then again be a hard, congealed mass; take this out. Take as much of it as the mercury you added to it, and use it to transform metals according to your pleasure. And when the mass is ground down, add the same amount of mercury again—namely, the 50th part—and keep it again for 30 days in the heat as before. Then take the medicine out again and add mercury once more. Carry this on for as long as you live, and you shall have an **increase** <term>Augment</term>, a refuge for performing **projections** <note>original: *proijcieren*; the final transformation of base metal into gold</note> in your time of need.

## The Fourth Part.
### The Precise Preparation of the Mineral Stone. <note>original: *Accuratio Lapidis Mineralis*</note>

To assemble the **Mineral Stone** quickly, proceed as follows: Make a **strong water** <term>Aqua fortis</term> <note>a powerful acidic solvent, usually nitric acid</note> from two pounds of calcined **vitriol** <note>iron or copper sulfate used to create acids</note>, one pound of saltpeter <note>OCR cut off: *Salpeter*</note>, and one and a half pounds of **cinnabar** <note>a bright red mineral consisting of mercury sulfide</note>. When it has been distilled as is customary, always add one and a half pounds of fresh cinnabar to each pound of the water and distill it again. Do this five times, so that you have incorporated three pounds of cinnabar into one pound of water. Once this is done, take one pound of the strong water that has been sharpened with cinnabar, and one pound of **Moonwort** <term>Lunariæ</term> <note>an alchemical herb or substance often associated with silver or lunar properties</note> that has been purified in the best way with **Salt of Tartar** <term>Sale Tartari</term> <note>potassium carbonate, used as a flux or purifying agent</note>. Mix these together very gently; let it stand for one or two days in a warm **water bath** <term>Balneo</term> so that they incorporate well with one another, and then distill them together.

<margin>
This salt is more noble than the Salt of Tartar. <note>original Latin: *Hoc Sal nobilius Sale Tartari*</note>
</margin>

If you now wish to make the **Vegetable Salt** <term>Sal Vegetabile</term>, circulate the mixture for 16 days in the water bath until it unites at the bottom of the glass like a crystalline glass. Keep that and use it in the Mineral Stone in place of the **Philosophical Ointment** <term>Vnguentum Philosophicum</term>. Put your calcined gold into it—add one ounce of gold for every twelve ounces of the salt—and set it to **putrefy** <note>the stage of "rotting" or breaking down the material, often resulting in a black color</note> for 20 days. Also add one ounce of the Philosophical Ointment, and it will become pure water. Afterwards, place a distillation head <note>original: *Helm*</note> upon it and draw off the water in the water bath, so that only the gold and whatever the water leaves behind remain at the bottom. Congeal <note>solidify</note> this in the **ashes** <note>a sand or ash bath used for gentle, even heating</note>. When it has cooled well and you have opened the glass, weigh the material and add an equal weight of the aforementioned cinnabar mixture and a very little Philosophical Ointment. Dissolve it again in the water bath and congeal it in the ashes. Do this ten times. Then take your dissolved powder; for every one ounce of powder, add twelve ounces of the best rectified Moonwort, prepared with Salt of Tartar and gold, and one ounce of calcined gold or sulfur. Put it all through the process of putrefaction; place it in a **Hermetic vessel** <term>Vas Hermetis</term> <note>a glass flask sealed airtight by melting the neck</note>, let it pass through the **colors** <note>the sequence of color changes—usually black, white, and red—that signal progress in the Alchemical Work</note> for 22 days, and fix it <note>render it stable and non-volatile</note> if it is not already finished by that time. However, I expect that you will complete it in 10 or, at the longest, 12 days.

When this is done, take this **Medicine** <note>another term for the Alchemical Stone or its intermediate stages</note>: for every ounce, take half an ounce of the Philosophical Ointment and putrefy them together for nine days in the water bath. Afterwards, congeal it in the ashes, then dissolve it again by itself without any addition, and congeal it. Continue this until it no longer allows itself to be dissolved. Then you have enough, and you can finish this Medicine in 80 days.

# On the Universal and Particular Path <note>original: *In Via Vniuersali & Particulari*</note>

### Multiplication of the Medicine <note>original: *Multiplicatio Medicinæ*</note>

Multiply this **Medicine** <note>in alchemy, the "Medicine" refers to the Elixir or the Philosopher's Stone, capable of "healing" base metals into gold</note> as follows: Take one ounce of this **Stone** in a glass, and lay upon it half an ounce of the **amalgam** <term>Amalgama</term> <note>a blend of metals, in this case gold and mercury</note> that is made from one part gold and five parts **mercury** <term>Mercurij</term>. Seal the glass with a **blind helm** <note>a still-head without a spout, used for refluxing or circulating vapors back into the vessel</note>; place it in warm ashes for six hours. When the material looks like gold, then stop; if not, then continue with the fire until you see the sign, or until it turns into a red powder. Then take again a little of the **Philosophical Ointment** <term>Vnguento Philosophico</term> <note>a fatty or oily substance produced during the alchemical process, used as a solvent</note>, add it to this powder to **dissolve** <term>solvieren</term> it, and **congeal** <term>congeliers</term> <note>turning a liquid back into a solid through cooling or evaporation</note> it again in the ashes. Repeat this until it will no longer allow itself to be congealed.

Then take one part of this last **Medicine**; add it again to ten parts of the **amalgam** in a sealed glass; dissolve it and congeal it. From that same Medicine take one part again, add it to ten parts of the amalgam, or to common mercury, and do with it as before. Continue with this repetition for so long and so many times until it no longer becomes a red powder but rather a hard, brittle mass. Then cast some of it <note>perform a "projection" or test</note> and pay attention to how much it **tinges** <note>the transformative power of the stone to "color" or change the nature of another metal</note>. Thus you will find the right **proportion** <note>original: *Proporß*</note>: how many parts of mercury or of the **imperfect metals** <note>base metals like lead, tin, or copper</note> you may tinge with one part of this Medicine, so that it becomes eternal, stable gold, as good as that which comes from the mines.

But if you wish to perform a **multiplication** that proceeds forever without end, then take some of the last Medicine or **congealment** <note>original: *Congelation*</note> where the mass has become hard. Grind it up, then take 50 parts by weight of common mercury (relative to the weight of the mass), put them together in a well-secured glass, and let it stand in a steady, small, gentle heat for 30 days. Then it will once again be a hard, congealed mass; take this out. Take as much from it as the mercury you added to it, and **tinge** with it according to your pleasure. And when the mass is ground up, then add as much mercury to it again—namely, the 50th part—and keep it again for 30 days in the heat as before. Then take the Medicine out again and add more mercury. Continue this for as long as you live, and you shall have an **increase** <note>original: *Augment*</note>, a refuge to **project** <term>proijcieren</term> <note>the act of casting the stone upon base metal to transform it</note> in your time of need.

# Report on Alchemy <note>original: *Bericht von der Alchemey*</note>

...half a pound of cinnabar <note>original: *Zinober*; mercury sulfide</note>; putrefy it day and night in a water bath <note>original: *Balneo*</note>, then set it in sand and burn it into a strong water <note>original: *Aqua fortis*; usually nitric acid</note> as is customary. Afterward, add fresh vitriol <note>sulfate minerals</note> and cinnabar in the previous proportion to the water; treat it as before. Do this five times. Then take one ounce of gold, which has been calcined <note>reduced to a fine powder through heat</note> most subtly by means of common mercury <note>original: *Mercurium Vulgi*</note>, and afterward made volatile by the calcined volatile water <note>original: *Wasser Volatile*</note>. Place this into twelve ounces of this strong water; set it to putrefy for twenty days in a water bath.

After such time, take it out, and thus it is resolved <note>dissolved into liquid form</note>. Take that, place a helm <note>a distillation cap</note> upon it, and gently draw off the water so that nothing remains behind but the gold and what the water leaves behind—a mass as large as the gold—remaining in the glass. To this, add one ounce of **Philosophical Ointment** <note>original: *Vnguenti Philosophici*; a refined alchemical substance, often fatty or oily in consistency</note>; set it for two days in putrefaction, then dry it in ashes <note>original: *in Cinere*; a gentle heat source</note>. After that, add some of the aforementioned strong water—no more than the amount of powder remaining in the glass—putrefy it for one day and night, and dry it in the ashes. Do this ten times.

After this, add twelve ounces of strong water, an ounce and a half of **Philosophical Ointment**, and one ounce of calcined gold or sulfur <note>original: *Sulphuris*</note> to the aforementioned powder. Set it for six days in a water bath to putrefy, then afterward in a circulating vessel <note>original: *Circulatorium*</note> or Hermetic vessel <note>original: *Vas Hermetis*; a glass vessel sealed with heat</note>. Let it stand in the ashes for ten or twelve days until it remains at the bottom like a stone and no longer rises upward. Then dissolve it by itself, or with a little **Philosophical Ointment** in a water bath; congeal it in ashes, dissolve it again, and congeal it. Do this three times, or until it no longer allows itself to be congealed but remains like an oil. Thus you have perfectly made the **Medicine**, which is a mixture of mineral and vegetable; with this, you may tincture <note>transform base metals into gold or silver</note> as mentioned above. And this Medicine, which the authors have made before, is prepared in eight days.

Separate the water from it in the philosophical manner, for the first form is water. Set aside the earth <note>the solid residue</note> that remains behind in this distillation, and divide the drawn-off water into two parts. # Garden of Riches <note>original Latin: *Hortus Diuitiarum*</note>

Seeking the art receptively; this part, which primarily deals with the secrets and the most hidden mysteries of the other **Astronomy** <note>In alchemy, "Astronomy" often refers to the study of "celestial" or volatile influences within chemical substances.</note> and the other **Philosophy**, likewise the experience of **Blessed Alchemy**: how through the help of this art, natures are to be brought to perfection. Therein I will show you flowers of all kinds of colors in this whole world, such as you might ever imagine. And in particular, I will teach you to assemble and mix certain roots of nature—the noblest of all—and the herbs which are the most secret in the art of the **Philosophical Mastery** <note>original: *Magisterij*; the "Great Work" or the achievement of the alchemical goal.</note>. I will teach you to separate and preserve their fragrant flowers, and also to extract their delicious juice and marrow in the purest way. And lastly, I will teach you to perfectly confirm and **fix** <note>original: *figieren*; to make a substance stable so it no longer evaporates or changes when heated.</note> all of this, so that henceforth no element can harm or spoil it. Rather, let it be something that takes root in the fire, grows in the air, shows its leaves in the water, and turns green in the earth, and multiplies itself at all times so that none of its power is lost.

Once you have collected these and tasted their sweetness, they will protect you from hunger and thirst. They will give you an abundance of **riches** which will never again be lacking. They heal and **preserve** <note>original: *præservieren*</note> you from all diseases and keep your life in a healthy state for a long duration, according to the will of God.

# Chapter One

## On the Knowledge and Revelation of the Matter and substances of the Philosophers, from which the highest Masterpiece <note>original: *Magisterium*; in alchemy, this refers to the ultimate goal or the completed Philosophers' Stone.</note> of the Philosophers’ Stone is made.

Take heed, you sons, and recognize the natural roots and the noblest herbs of the Philosophers. Their roots are green, mixed with a whiteness; but their herbs are of brown, red, and white color, while some are yellowish. Their flowers, scent, and taste are so noble that nothing sweeter, nothing stronger, or more precious in this world can be found that might equal them in goodness. Their extracted juice also takes on various colors, for it becomes red in the sunlight, and in the brightness of light, it turns to the whiteness of the moon <note>In alchemical symbolism, "the moon" represents Silver or the "White Work" (Albedo).</note>. And these herbs are quite common—a heavenly gift found at all times and in all places, possessed by the rich as well as the poor. They are simple and rejected, and are used least of all for our medicine; for their virtues are hidden. The ancients never wished to reveal anything about them, but instead kept them most hidden. Whose names I have fully stated, and I swear by the Creator of Heaven and Earth that from them alone the Art is completed, and from no other thing in this entire world.

Therefore, I most earnestly plead with all those who, through God's grace, shall draw understanding from this book and receive its fruit, that they do not use or enjoy such a Divine gift for evil, haughtiness, pride, or a tyrannical life. But rather, praise and honor God, and share it for the benefit of the body and the salvation of the soul, so that the poor and needy may receive comfort and help, and thus cry out together to the Heavenly Almighty God. This I ask so that I might not be found among those of wicked life at the Last Judgment, and that the wrath of the stern Judge does not crush me along with them, but that I may hear His lovely voice with the chosen ones: "Come here, you blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom," <note>Matthew 25:34; a common scriptural citation in alchemical texts to emphasize the practitioner's moral duty.</note> etc.

# The Second Chapter
## On the Labor of the Blessed Stone.

My son, now lay your hands to the work, and say in the name of GOD: O GOD, help me, protect me, and grant me your grace.
Therefore, take all herbs that are known to you, with their roots and flowers, and extract from them the four elements in this way. Take a good portion of the mentioned herbs, of each an equal part <note>original: *ana*; a medical and alchemical term meaning "of each an equal amount"</note>. Grind this earth finely, pour over it its own extracted water, and sublimate it again as at first. <margin>7 times</margin> Do this seven times—that is, let the dead rise seven times; meaning they kill themselves seven times through rising <note>In alchemy, "rising" or evaporation is often equated with the spirit leaving the body, or "dying"</note>, and become living again seven times through descending. For when Father Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note>, who was a King of the Greeks, was asked what the most important thing in the Art was, he said: "That the dead rise seven times, and the living descend seven times." Thus you will have what you seek. This venerable water, which is called a Fountain of Life, you shall sublimate by itself <note>original Latin: *per se*</note> two or three times. Cast away the earth or dregs <term>Fæces: the solid waste or residue left after distillation</term> which it leaves at the bottom in each sublimation. Thereafter, sublimate it again by itself, slowly, with a mild fire, until the substance of the water is entirely extracted. Keep this blessed oil and liquid <term>Liquor: a fluid substance</term> of the philosophers in a clean vessel, well-sealed.

## The Fourth Chapter.
### On the Form and Shape of the Vessel in which the Material is Cooked.

For the Stone there is only one vessel in which the entire Great Work <note>original: *Magisterium*, referring to the completion of the Philosopher's Stone</note> is perfected. This is a blind cucurbit <note>term: A gourd-shaped glass vessel; "blind" means it has no opening at the top or its opening is sealed</note> which has no lid. It is a single vessel made of glass, thick and well-annealed <note>The process of slow cooling to toughen the glass</note>: sealed on all sides, half a cubit <note>roughly 9 to 12 inches in this context</note> long, and round or flat at the top, of a good width. It should be slightly curved at the bottom, and the sides should be brought up straight, far enough apart from each other so that whatever is sublimated <note>term: Sublimation is the process where a substance is heated into vapor and then solidifies again at the top of the vessel</note> can rise and fall without hindrance.

The way to seal <note>original: *sigillieren*, likely referring to the "Seal of Hermes" or an airtight glass seal</note> the vessel is as follows. First, take the previously mentioned *Philosophical* divided water, well mixed with its noble earth and its fresh blood, and place it into its suitable glass, the shape of which has been described. Then close the mouth of the glass in this manner: Take a glass ball and place it upon the mouth of the glass vessel; around it, sprinkle crushed glass. Then place the glass or flask into a pot and put ash around it so that the ash is two finger-breadths thick on all sides. The flask should extend about two fingers' width above the ash, or a little more. Then surround it with coals and let them catch fire. When the neck of the glass glows red, sprinkle a little borax <note>original: *Burras*; used here as a flux to lower the melting point of the glass</note> onto the ball, and the glass will flow immediately <note>fusing the ball to the neck to create a permanent seal</note>. Then let it cool and take out the vessel with the material inside. Note always that you should weigh the glass before the material is put inside, so that you know how to adjust your measurements if you wish to add more.

# The Third Chapter.
## On the Division of the Philosophical Water, and its Nobility.

<margin>1st part.</margin>
Son, turn yourself around and look into the expanse of my garden, and pay attention to the Living Fountain that takes its origin from the foundation of the noblest Philosophical extracted blossoms and their divided, miraculous flowers. This is the fountain of living water, for it is the fountain of joy, of youth, of beauty, and of health. To the water that springs forth and flows out of the fountain, such power and virtue has been given by God that its praise, its honor, and its refreshment <note>original: *erckung*, likely *Erquickung*</note> cannot be fully explained by all the philosophers.

<margin>Gottfried. Is v.</margin>
One reads in Genesis <note>original: *Genesi*</note> in the first [chapter] that the Spirit <note>original: *Spiritus*</note> of the Lord hovered over the water in the creation of Heaven and Earth. Therefore, know that everything is made out of water. God has divided this water, speaking and commanding that one part of the water should become a dryness, and such He called the Earth. The remaining water, which was not divided, He kept to water and to moisten. For the dry earth gives no fruit unless it were moistened from above with its rain water. Thus I reveal to you, in a natural way, the secrets <note>original: *Verborgenhert*, likely *Verborgenheit*</note> of the Philosophical Stone: namely, that you divide it into two parts, <margin>1st part: garment <note>original: *gwand*</note></margin> each part well-sealed in its vessel. Coagulate <note>term: *coagulirt*; the alchemical process of thickening a liquid into a solid</note> the one part <margin>2nd part: keep p. 294</margin> and turn it into earth; keep the other part to bedew, to imbibe <note>term: *imbiberen*; to saturate a solid with liquid until it can absorb no more</note>, and to wax <note>term: *incerieren*; from *inceration*, the process of softening a substance to a wax-like consistency</note> the dried-out part of the water.

# The Fourth Chapter /
## On the Form and Shape of the Vessel in which the Matter is Cooked.

For the Stone <note>the Philosopher's Stone</note>, there is only one vessel in which the entire <term>Magisterium</term> <note>the "Mastery" or the completed alchemical process</note> is perfected. And it is a blind <term>Cucurbit</term> <note>a gourd-shaped glass vessel</note> which has no lid. It is a single vessel made of glass, thick and well-annealed <note>cooled slowly to remove internal stresses</note>: sealed on all sides, half a cubit <note>about 12 inches or 30 cm</note> long, and round or flat at the top. It should be of a good width: the bottom should be slightly curved, and the sides should be brought up straight and far enough apart from each other so that whatever is sublimated <note>turned into vapor by heat</note> can rise and descend without hindrance.

***

# The Fifth Chapter /
## How to Seal the Vessels.

<margin>retained e. divided W. p. 504. <unclear>Beit</unclear></margin>
The way to seal <note>original: *sigillieren*; to hermetically close</note> the vessels happens thus. First, take the aforementioned Philosophical divided water, well-mixed with its noble earth and its fresh blood; place it into its suitable glass, the shape of which has been described, and then close the mouth of the glass as follows: Take a cast sphere, lay it upon the mouth-hole of the glass, and strew crushed glass around it. Then place the glass or flask <note>original: *Kolben*</note> into a pot. Put ashes around it so that they are two finger-breadths thick all around. The flask should extend about two finger-breadths above the ashes, or a little more. Then surround it with coals and let them catch fire. When the neck of the glass glows, strew a little <term>Borax</term> <note>original: *Burras*; used as a flux to help the glass melt together</note> onto the sphere, and the glass will flow immediately. Then let it cool and take out the vessel with the matter inside. Always remember to weigh the glass before you put the matter in, so that you know how to proceed if you wish to add more.

# The Sixth Chapter /
## On the Philosophical Furnace / and how the vessel should be placed.

Have a vessel made for yourself out of good fire-resistant clay, in which you will arrange our Old One <note>a symbolic name for the prime matter or the Stone</note> or Stone, or Sealed Water. This clay vessel should be of such a width that the glass fits comfortably inside, and so that about three finger-breadths of ashes can be filled in all around it. Over the mentioned vessel, have a lid made of the same clay, so that the fire does not touch or strike the glass vessel containing the Matter; set this one atop the other. At the top of this lid, have another small lid made with a handle, which you can lift off if it becomes necessary to look at the Matter. Now, we place the Matter into the coated <note>original: *beschlagenen*; likely "luted" or coated with a protective layer of clay</note> glass, and then into the aforementioned earthen vessel. The glass should be three or four parts empty, and only one part full.

Construct the furnace in the following way: Prepare a good loam <note>a mixture of clay, sand, and straw</note>, mixed with horse manure and sand, and well-worked so that it may better hold the heat. Make a round structure, two spans <note>about 18 inches or 45 cm</note> in width and two spans in height. In the middle of this, a base should be placed which has a hole in the center, through which you can slide a fist, so that the air may draw through it. Above the mentioned base, an iron piece should be inset with a cross, from which the lamp <note>original: *Ampel*; a steady oil lamp used as a heat source</note> shall hang. This should be in a gap where, between the lamp and the furnace walls, a fist may be pushed through on all sides, or four finger-breadths, so that the air can circulate.

Upon this furnace, set another furnace, into which iron bars are placed so that the earthen vessel (containing the glass with the Matter) can be set upon them. Such bars should be set one standard foot <note>original: *Werckschuch*</note> high above the base. The height of this furnace should be raised up to the lid of the lower earthen vessel that stands on the bars: the reason for this is so that when you want to look at the Matter to see how the <term>signs</term> <note>original: *Signa* or *Warzeichen*; the specific color changes, like the Black Sun or White Swan, that indicate progress</note> manifest themselves, there is no hindrance as there would be if the furnace were too high. The width of this part of the furnace should be such that there are four finger-breadths of space between the vessel and the walls, so that the heat of the fire does not only strike the bottom of the lower vessel in which the glass with the Matter stands, but rather [spreads] itself all around

# The Seventh Chapter /
## On the Philosophical Wick.

The lamp should be placed under the glass, and it must burn without ceasing. For <term>the</term> <note>original: *dz* (abbreviation for *das*)</note> Philosophical Fire is made with a wick of three threads, and no more: they should also not be too coarse. But the Philosophical Wick <note>often described in alchemical texts as an "asbestos" or "everlasting" wick that does not consume itself</note> never burns away, nor is it consumed, so that the worker needs to do nothing else but pour in more oil. With such a fire our work is completed, and not otherwise. Therefore, take care that it does not go out.

---

# The Eighth Chapter /
## On the Degrees of Fire, how they are to be governed throughout the entire work.

Maintaining the governance of the fire is no small skill. For in the <term>Solution</term> <note>the process of dissolving a solid into a liquid state</note>, the fire should always be gentle; in the <term>Sublimation</term> <note>the process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then collects as a solid again</note>, moderate; in the <term>Coagulation</term> <note>the thickening or hardening of the liquid matter</note>, tempered; in the Whiteness <note>the *Albedo* stage</note>, increasing; and in the Redness <note>the *Rubedo* or final stage</note>, strong.

If you err in these through ignorance, you will often regret your loss. However, the more the colors change, the more the fire is to be increased gently, until it attains the signs of Whiteness. This Whiteness requires much fire because it is moist and cold, and is poorly "cooked." <note>Alchemists viewed the transformation of matter as a process of "digestion" or "cooking" driven by heat</note> For this reason, the female figures...

# The Tenth Chapter /

Be told, dear son, you should know that in this single closed glass, in a single cooking, seven dispositions and orders are accomplished for this **Great Work**. The first is **Decay** <note>original: *Putrefactio*</note>, so that you may extract a pure, subtle substance; The second is **Dissolution** <note>original: *Solutio*</note>, so that the entire matter is dissolved into a water; The third is **Decay** <note>original: *Putrefactio*</note>; The fourth is a **Washing** or **Purification** <note>original: *Ablutio*</note>; The fifth is **Coagulation** <note>original: *Coagulatio*</note>, which is to gently dry the water into our Sun; The sixth is **Calcination** <note>original: *Calcinatio*; reducing a solid to a fine powder using heat</note>; The seventh is **Fixation** <note>original: *Fixatio*; the process of making a volatile substance stable in fire</note>. But in these seven orders, seven other common changes of nature manifest, which appear wonderful to the sight. For when our stone is placed in our vessel and finds the warmth of the sun, it immediately dissolves itself into a water. At times it rises upward into the height of the vessel, and thereafter it falls back down again to the **bottom of the vessel** <note>original Latin: *ad Fundum deß Geschirrs*</note>; And through

# The Eleventh Chapter /
## Concerning the manifold colors which appear during the governance.

NOTICE, there are three principal colors which appear in the Work: **Black**, **White**, and **Red**. Alongside these, there are also other colors that allow themselves to be seen in the Work: The first is silver-colored; the second, Black; the third, Multi-colored; the fourth, Brown; the fifth, Green; the sixth, Mirrored, like the **Peacock’s Feathers** <note>known in Latin as the *Cauda Pavonis*, this stage of shimmering colors indicates that the "Blackness" is breaking and the transition to "Whiteness" is beginning</note>; the seventh, toward silver-white; the eighth, the highest perfect Whiteness; the ninth, Brown; the tenth, Saffron-colored; the eleventh, the perfect Redness; and many other colors come in between, to which one need not pay much attention.

# The Fifteenth Chapter
## On the Fermentation of the Blessed Stone.

Take five or six parts of the completed and perfectly fixed white or red **Medicine** <term>Medicine: a common alchemical term for the Philosopher's Stone in its potent, transformative state</term>, and one part of the white or red **prepared Body** <note>original: *præprirten Corporis*</note>, most purely and well **calcined** <note>calciniert: the process of heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to a fine powder</note>. Place them together in a **Fixing-Glass** <note>original: *Figier-Glaß*</note> to **putrefy** <note>putreficieren: to rot or decompose, a necessary stage of breakdown before rebirth</note> in the **Mary’s Bath** <note>original: *Balneo Mariæ*; a water bath used for gentle, indirect heating</note> within the **Philosophical Oven**; govern the fire with due measure until that which was first made **volatile** <note>Volatile: a substance that easily evaporates or changes state</note> takes unto itself the **fixed Body** <note>Fix Corpus</note>, so that the **fixed becomes volatile**, and the **volatile becomes fixed**. And when you see the appearance of many colors, strengthen the fire until you find everything **fixed** in the form of an oil; then you have the true **Elixir**, with which you can **tincture** <note>tingieren: to transform or "dye" base metals into gold or silver</note> whenever you wish.

And note that you do not need to perform this **fermentation** more than once. For the entire **matter** <note>Matery</note> transforms itself into a **ferment**; therefore you do not need to start anew again. For just as the **leaven** <note>Heffel: yeast or sourdough starter</note> of bread changes or sours the whole dough, so from this **paste** <note>Past</note> a portion is kept as a **ferment** to again **ferment** another **paste**, and this is again as noble as before. That is the property in the **philosophical matter**.

---

## That the Tincture is increased through Solution, and also through Fermentation.

Our **Medicine** is increased through **solution** <note>Solution: the process of dissolving a solid into a liquid</note> and also through **fermentation**. Through **solution**, it is somewhat slower; but through **fermentation**, our **Medicine** is much more quickly **augmented** <note>augmentiert: increased in quantity or potency</note>. For if it is not **dissolved** <note>solviert</note>, it does not **operate** <note>operiert</note> well, unless it be fixed in its ferment. It

The **Philosophers** <note>The "Philosophers" refers to the historical alchemical authorities and masters of the craft</note> are of many different opinions regarding the **augmentation** and **fermentation** of the Stone, whether for the White <note>the stage for silver-making</note> or the Red <note>the stage for gold-making</note>. <margin>
Of the red water reserved. See page 511.
</margin>
It is likewise to be noted that the **Elixir** can be **augmented** and increased in two ways, namely in volume and quantity, and in quality and power. In volume or quantity, it is **augmented** as follows: Take one part of the red reserved water and three parts of the **Elixir**; put them together and arrange everything in its proper philosophical vessel, and place it again over a gentle fire until it turns into a **Stone** <note>original Latin: *Lapidem*</note>.

Some arrange it in a **cucurbit** <term>Cucurbit: a gourd-shaped glass vessel that forms the lower part of a distillation apparatus</term>, pouring over it the first **rectified** <note>purified through distillation</note> water, with its **helm** <note>the cap or "alembic" that sits atop the cucurbit</note> placed upon it and well **luted** <note>sealed with an airtight paste or clay</note>. Then it is placed in the furnace, its **receiver** <note>original: *Fürschlag*; the vessel that catches the distilled liquid</note> also well luted, and with a gentle fire, as is necessary, they draw all the water away from it. Then they pour the water back over it and draw it off again, repeating this so often until they see the aforementioned **matter** at the **bottom** <note>original Latin: *in Fundo*</note> of the vessel shining brightly, like a naked sword, and brought back to its former Whiteness or Redness, according to how the **matter** was **prepared**. And this is a higher and more hidden **secret** than can be believed.

## The Eighteenth Chapter,
### How the Medicine is augmented in quality.

In quality, the **Elixir** is augmented thus: namely, that one takes <note>original: *ne-* / *nehme*</note> of the **volatile Stone**, which has the **nature of a woman** <note>In alchemical theory, "female nature" refers to the volatile, cold, or moist principle, typically associated with Mercury</note>, three [parts], and of the **Elixir** one part. Put these together as is necessary; place them in a **cucurbit** <term>cucurbit: a gourd-shaped glass vessel used in distillation</term>. Over this, if you wish, pour some of the [red] water so that it swims above it. **Seal** <term>seal: hermetically sealing the vessel (often called the Seal of Hermes) to prevent the spirit from escaping</term> it according to custom; arrange it in the furnace with its **receiver** <note>the vessel that catches the distilled liquid</note>, the joints also being well **luted** <term>luted: sealed with a specialized airtight clay or paste</term>. **Distill** the water with a gentle fire, and when it has completely come over, then strengthen the fire so that everything that wishes to **sublime** <term>sublime: the process where a solid substance is turned into vapor by heat and then cools back into a solid at the top of the vessel</term> may rise up.

That which is **sublimed**, add it back to that **at the bottom** <note>original: *in Fundo*</note>, as was previously reiterated and [sublimed?], as many times as necessary, until through such repeated **sublimation** [the whole] remains **at the bottom**.

When it has all become **fixed** <term>fixed: a stable state where the substance can no longer be evaporated or changed by fire</term> in this way, then add again its quantity of the **volatile Stone**, and **imbibe** <note>to "imbibe" is to gradually add liquid to a dry substance until it is saturated</note> it in the aforementioned way, until everything rises up again and finally becomes fixed once more. Continue this until it flows quite easily, exactly like wax. This **Medicine** is constant; it **tinges** <term>tinge: the transformative power of the Stone to color and change the nature of a metal</term>, penetrates, consolidates, and makes [the metal] resistant [to fire]. One part of this **transmutes** a thousand times a thousand parts of any **body** <note>original: *Corpore*</note> into true **Gold** or **Silver**.

## The Nineteenth Chapter,
### How the Medicine shall be fermented at the last,
### so that it may perfectly tinge.

But when you wish to **tinge**, take of the same **body** <note>original: *Corpore*</note> with which you have **fermented** in your work—namely, whether it be **White** <note>for making silver</note> or **Red** <note>for making gold</note>. Bring this **body** into a **subtle lime** <note>a fine powder produced through calcination or heating</note>; lay it in a **luted** dish or in a crucible over the fire, and drip the **oil of the Elixir** onto it little by little, so that the powder may take it in, and together they may become a **subtle powder**. Take care that not too much of the oil is lost upon it. This **Ferment** is the **Elixir**, with which you can **tinge** all metals and **quicksilver** <note>original: *Argentum uuum* / *vivum*</note> into **Silver** or **Gold**, according to how the **Medicine** has been prepared.

## How the Medicine is augmented in Quality.

Put them together as is required and place them in a **cucurbit** <term>Cucurbit: a gourd-shaped glass vessel used for distillation</term>. Distill the water with a gentle fire; and when it has completely come over, then strengthen the fire so that everything that wishes to **sublimate** <term>Sublimation: the process where a solid is heated into a vapor and then collected again as a solid</term> may rise up.

Take that which has sublimated and return it to the residue at the **bottom** <note>original: "in Fundo"</note>, repeating and sublimating as before, time after time, until through such repeated sublimation everything remains at the bottom.

When it has all become **fixed** <term>Fixation: the process of making a volatile substance stable under heat so it no longer evaporates</term> in this way, then add again its quantity of the Volatile Stone and **imbibe** <term>Imbibition: the slow addition of liquid to a dry substance until it is fully saturated</term> it in the aforementioned way, until it all rises again and finally becomes fixed once more. Continue this until it flows as easily as wax. This **Medicine** is enduring; it **tinges** <term>Tingeing: the alchemical transformation of a metal's color and nature into gold or silver</term>, penetrates, consolidates, and makes stable. One part of this transmutes a thousand times a thousand <note>i.e., one million parts</note> of any body into true gold or silver.

Bring this Body into a subtle **calx** <term>Calx: a fine powder produced by heating a metal to a very high temperature (calcination)</term>; place it in a luted glass dish or in a crucible over the fire, and drip the **Oil of the Elixir** onto it little by little, so that the powder absorbs it and they become one subtle powder together. Guard yourself against using too much of the oil. This **Ferment** is the Elixir with which you can tinge all metals and **Quicksilver** <note>original: "Argentum Vivum"</note> into silver or gold, according to how the Medicine was prepared.

->### Garden of Riches.###<-

In the manner of making crystals flow, and adding the powder into it, it will change them into a ruby. Afterward, let glass flow with the mentioned powder, and it will become malleable and allow itself to be hammered. When all this has been done, and you have accomplished it, you should say: "This is the glory and majesty of my Lord."

Afterward, you shall further explain my <term>Magisterium</term> <note>The "Mastery" or the ultimate alchemical achievement/substance</note>: One should give it to the most unclean lepers to drink; whereupon they shall immediately lie down and cover themselves with sweat-cloths; they will soon become healthy, so that it will seem to them that they no longer walk upon the earth, but float in the air. Therefore, depart now in peace, and fulfill my longing and desire.

When this man departed with joy, he found the aforementioned things to be true in reality, and demonstrated such to the Pope and the Emperor. Thus, the <term>Philosophical Medicine</term> <note>A term for the Philosopher's Stone emphasizing its power to heal both metals and humans</note> was proven before the highest Bishop <note>original: "höchsten Bischoff," referring to the Pope</note> and before the Emperor who reigned at that time: that it has the power to heal and cure human sickness, and to transmute all imperfect <term>bodies</term> (<term>Corpora</term> <note>In alchemical theory, the "bodies" are the seven base metals</note>) into perfection, and to transmute all raw, coarse stones into precious, noble gemstones; also to make glass malleable under the hammer. May the grace, virtue, and effect of the Almighty and Holy Trinity grant and impart such to every true-believing person who seeks this medicine, Amen.

Praise and honor and eternal thanks be said to God the Father, and His only-begotten Son, and God the Holy Spirit—the Trinity and the one reigning Lord and God—from eternity to eternity, Amen.

For it is given solely out of your inexhaustible grace. ### and is divided into Twelve Chapters.

## The First Chapter,
### How one should sublimate the Mercury for the Art.

Also take 2 pounds of <term>Vitriol</term> <note>Sulfate minerals, usually green or blue vitriol, used as acidic reagents</note>, one pound of <term>Mercury</term> <note>Quicksilver</note>, and one pound of common salt. Sublimate it thus for the first time, and for the second and third times. For the fourth time, through common salt, and for the fifth time, by itself alone.

## The Second Chapter,
### How one should turn the prepared sublimated Mercury into water.

Also take pure, fine <term>Tin</term> <note>Represented by the symbol ♃</note> and common Mercury, one pound of each; from these, make an <term>Amalgam</term> <note>A mixture or alloy of mercury with another metal</note>. Wash the amalgam thoroughly until the blackness is removed, and dry it well over gentle heat. And take two pounds of the <term>sublimated Mercury</term> <note>The mercury purified in the previous chapter</note>, or as much as the weight of the amalgam, and grind them together on a smooth stone. Place it on a glass plate in a damp cellar that is warm; thus, a "water" [liquid] will form from it. Distill this—if it comes down cloudy—through a filter, and put it into a glass vessel. Place it in horse manure <note>A common alchemical method for providing gentle, consistent biological heat</note> or in a <term>Bain-marie</term> <note>original: "Balneum Mariæ," a water bath</note> for one month. Seal the glass very well so that it does not <insert>evaporate</insert> <note>original: "verrieche," literally "smell away" or lose its potency through scent</note>. Afterward, distill it through an <term>Alembic</term> <note>A distillation apparatus consisting of a gourd-shaped vessel and a cooling cap</note> into a glass receiver that is well <term>luted</term> <note>sealed with airtight clay or paste</note>. Distill it from the water bath, and then distill it further from the ash [an ash-bath] with gentle fire, and keep this well-sealed for your work. And the <term>residue</term> <note>original: "Fæces," the solid remains left after distillation</note> that remained in the glass, keep that also well-protected and <term>calcine</term> <note>heat to a high temperature to reduce to a powder</note> it, as will be seen hereafter in the Sixth Chapter.

## The Sixth Chapter/
### How one should prepare the Middle, that is Tin.

<margin>p. 523.</margin>
Likewise, take the "Middle"/ that is <term>tin</term> <note>alchemists often referred to metals by symbolic rankings; tin was frequently the "middle" between base lead and precious silver</note>/ and <term>calcine</term> <note>to reduce a metal to a powder (oxide) through intense heat; original: "calcinier"</note> it until it becomes white. After that, <term>reduce</term> it/ or let it flow/ with <term>saltpeter</term> <note>potassium nitrate; original: "Saliter"</note> and <term>olive oil</term> <note>literally "tree oil"; original: "Baumöl"</note>/ rubbing them together into a paste/ and then put it into a crucible/ and blow upon it with bellows/ and pour it out into a mold. One should always calcine it in this way/ and then let it flow again. At the third time, the tin is brought to its perfection. At the fourth time, calcine it very well/ and dissolve it in <term>distilled spirits</term> <note>literally "burnt wine," an early term for brandy or high-proof alcohol; original: "Brannten Wein"/</note>, and thus the most noble part of the tin dissolves itself/ And when it is dissolved/ and has settled/ then distill it through a filter/ and draw the water off through an <term>alembic</term> <note>a distillation apparatus used for cooling and collecting vapors; original: "Alembicum"</note>, so that there remains at the bottom of the glass a stone like a crystal/ entirely transparent, of our nature. And that is the <term>Corpus</term> <note>the physical "body" of the substance</note>, with its pure, clarified, transparent spirit/ which is added in all measures/ and unites itself with it.

...[management] too [quickly] or slowly. But I want you to act in such a way that your thoughts follow Nature. And what sort of sign is there for the correct <term>Solution</term> <note>The process of dissolving a solid substance into a liquid state, often seen as the first step of the Great Work.</note> of the Stone? Answer: When the blackness first appears, that is a sign of the <term>Putrefaction</term> <note>original: Faulung. In alchemy, matter must "die" and decay (turn black) before it can be purified and reborn.</note> and Solution of the Stone.

Also, it is asked: Whether the black dregs in the aforementioned Stone remain or stay for 40 days? An answer: Yes, sometimes more, sometimes less. And the change happens because of the transformation of the scale of the <term>Intensity</term> <note>original: Ketzerey. While this word usually means "heresy," in this chemical context it likely refers to the "conflict" or "strife" of the reactive elements within the vessel.</note> and according to the skill of the operation.

## Separation of the Blackness.

<margin>Also</margin>
Also, it is asked: How long a time does the putrefaction and purification of the earth last? Answer: 40 days, sometimes more, sometimes less, according to the size of the work and the <term>Fire</term> <note>original: 🜄 (the alchemical symbol for the element of fire).</note>.

Afterward, pour one part of the water that has been precipitated with three parts <term>Distilled Wine</term> <note>original: "Brandten Wein"; a high-proof alcohol or brandy used as an alchemical solvent.</note>; thus the spirits of the water settle. Then place the matter on the little stove with a low fire, and gently draw off its moisture and the watery nature it has produced. Throw away the ninth water, and leave it under the blind alembic in the ashes, and maintain it in every way as before. Do this three or four times, until the water consumes itself without any boiling or bubbling, and let it stand under the blind alembic with a gentle fire, like the heat of the sun. Then the **Oil of the Stone** will be ready, with which one <term>tinctures</term> <note>To "tincture" means to transform or "dye" a base metal into a more perfect state, such as gold or silver.</note> the Mercury until the end.

### Another method, regarding Marcasite.

Take a measure of good vinegar and distill it. Let it stand in warmth until it turns yellow. Then pour off the yellow vinegar and pour another [fresh batch of vinegar] onto it. Do this until it no longer turns yellow. Afterward, take **calcined silver** <note>represented by the symbol ☽ (Moon/Silver).</note> and boil it out well, and pour the yellow vinegar upon it. Thus you have good **gold** <note>represented by the symbol ☉ (Sun/Gold).</note>.

-># The Second Tincture for White and Red.<-

The blessed Stone of the Sages, according to the content and the true natural way of the philosophers, as the same is prepared in the correct manner, art, and intention from the beginning until the end; also in every measure with complete truth, as I myself personally and quite truthfully found it to be in the Work. For the same is [not] prepared with sharp waters <note>Referencing corrosive acids like aqua fortis.</note> or substances contrary to nature, but only with, in, from, and not without the metals. For it must come from metals, from which metals are made, and from which metals can grow. For every tree brings forth its own seed and blossom, from which many beautiful apples or pears then grow and spring forth. Likewise, small branches are cut off which are fertile and have borne beautiful little growths, and come from a good tree. These are then set, planted, and grafted onto a wild, infertile trunk and stem; nevertheless, they are fertile as before, and teach that same infertile stem and trunk along with them, so that it becomes like them and likewise bears such fruit, just like these small branches. Thus, in the same manner, is it to be understood regarding the metals.

If you have a decayed, infertile, worthless metallic stem, and yet would like for that same stem not to perish entirely on account of its growing roots, then seek first for a small branch which bears beautiful and tasty fruit, either apples or pears. Take that same small branch and graft it very subtly, and at the right time, onto that stem—which usually happens in the spring—so that in summer it may bring forth its first green little leaves, grow in a little during the second summer and receive a strong trunk, but in the third summer it may usually bring its first fruit. Even if there is not much fruit, it is all the more flavorful and lovely to look upon, because it is the first fruit. Thus, henceforth, this tree of metals can bear more and more fruitfully as time and years go by, until at last its fruit becomes without number.

If it does not smoke and it flows like wax, it is correct and perfect. If it smokes, however, put it back in and let it stand until it becomes perfect.

Thus you have now prepared and brought the blessed <term>Philosopher's Stone</term> <note>original: *Stein der Weisse*; literally "Stone of the Wise."</note> to perfection. You will contemplate its multiplication yourself in a similar manner. But always give God praise and thanks for it, and remember the poor. Amen.

### The Cementation of Cinnabar.

First, calcine <term>vitriol</term> <note>original: *Victriolum*; iron or copper sulfate used as a powerful corrosive or drying agent.</note> until it becomes red. Then take it and put it into a vessel and pour a good strong vinegar over it; let it stand for two days, then let the vinegar run off through a cloth. Then place several small pieces of <term>cinnabar</term> <note>original: *Zinober*; mercury sulfide ore, known for its bright red color.</note> into the same vinegar, about the size of a die or a bit smaller, and let them lie therein for two nights and a day. Then take well-purified **silver** <note>original: ☾ (the astrological symbol for the Moon/Silver).</note> and file it small, and then arrange the mentioned <term>cinnabar</term> and **silver** in a glass, formed <term>layer upon layer</term> <note>original: *stratum super stratum*; a standard alchemical method of layering materials to ensure even reaction.</note> until the glass is half full, up to the point marked **A**. Then place the cap on top, well-sealed with lute <note>A specialized alchemical putty used to airtight-seal glassware.</note>. But see beforehand that the vinegar is well-dried from the cinnabar, otherwise the moisture will shatter the glass.

If you are not working on <term>Copper</term> <note>original: ♀</note>, you do not need this test.

### Sublimation of Mercury

Let Hungarian Vitriol <note>A sulfate mineral, likely copper or iron sulfate, used here as a reagent.</note> flow in a crucible until the moisture completely evaporates. # On the Stone in Mercurial Water

If you see forks or streaks appearing in the helm <note>The "helm" or *alembic* is the cooling cap of a still where vapors condense.</note>, stop immediately and discard what remains in the flask. Take fresh distilled wine again and proceed as before. Continue this until you have enough of the Quintessence <note>original: *Quint. Essent.*; the "fifth essence" or most purified spirit of a substance, in this case, highly concentrated alcohol.</note>.

Take the Quintessence you have just prepared and throw a good handful of dried salt into it. Distill it as before until you feel "sweet water" <note>This likely refers to a neutral taste, indicating that the spirituous part has already passed over.</note> on your tongue; then stop. Discard what remains in the distilling vessel. Take what you have distilled over, add another handful of salt, and distill it a third time until you feel sweet water; then stop. Again, discard the residue. Pour what has distilled over into a flask, add a handful of fresh Salt of Tartar <note>original: *Salis 🜖ri*</note>, and distill it completely over the "eighteenth stroke" <note>likely referring to a specific setting on a furnace or a measure of time</note>. Perform this process five times in succession.
